subjects.name: Histology
subjects.lectures: Tissue preparation, Microscopy, Staining and histochemistry

questions.text: The type of microscope used to detect movement of the mitochondria in culture is:
questions.explanation: Phase contrast reveals movement of living unstained mitochondria/cells in culture. Distinguishing alternatives: SEM images prepared surface specimens; TEM images thin prepared sections; Generic brightfield is less specific for unstained organelles; Electric microscope is not the required type.

questions.text: technique suitable for detection of enzymatic reactions & fat content is:
questions.explanation: Freezing avoids the heat/solvents that destroy enzymes and dissolve lipid in paraffin processing. Distinguishing alternatives: Paraffin loses lipids/enzymes; Plastic is used for EM preparation; Celloidin is not the stated rapid enzyme-preserving method.

questions.text: Metachromasia is a character of which of the following cells?
questions.explanation: Mast-cell granules change toluidine-blue staining to a metachromatic hue. Distinguishing alternatives: Fibroblasts lack these granules; Fat uses lipid stains; Plasma cells are basophilic; Macrophages use vital/enzyme stains.

questions.text: Trypan blue staining of macrophages is a .................. stain.
questions.explanation: Injected trypan blue is ingested by macrophages in the living body, a vital stain. Distinguishing alternatives: Neutral is dye chemistry; Acidic is dye chemistry; Histochemistry detects tissue chemistry; Supravital is outside-body living cells.

questions.text: Which of the following is TRUE about fixation?
questions.explanation: Fixation inhibits autolysis and putrefaction while hardening tissue and increasing stain affinity. Distinguishing alternatives: Putrefaction is prevented; Tissue hardens rather than loosens; Clearing makes tissue transparent; Mordanting increases rather than decreases.
options: It prevents post mortem degeneration and autolysis.
It allows the tissue to become transparent.
It makes the tissue less mordant

questions.text: Metachromasia is:
questions.explanation: Metachromasia means component colour differs from dye colour.
options: a stained tissue component with a color other than the color of dye.
a suitable technique for enzyme demonstration in the cells.
staining of living cells outside the body.
staining of living cells inside the living body.
used to differentiate between cells of the same origin.

questions.text: Hematoxylin stain is characterized by:
questions.explanation: Hematoxylin stains nucleic-acid-rich basophilic structures such as nucleus and rER blue-purple. Distinguishing alternatives: Hematoxylin acts as a basic staining system; It binds acidic rather than basic components; Muscle proteins are eosinophilic; Collagen red is eosin staining.

questions.text: Most suitable technique & staining for demonstration of enzymatic reactions:
questions.explanation: Frozen sections preserve enzyme activity, and enzyme histochemistry localizes its activity. Distinguishing alternatives: Immunostaining detects antigen rather than activity; Paraffin processing may destroy enzyme activity; Vital staining is not enzyme localization.

questions.text: The electron magnetic lenses that direct beam of electrons in EM include the following...
questions.explanation: TEM uses electromagnetic condenser, objective and projector lenses. Distinguishing alternatives: Eyepiece is a light-microscope component; Screen is not a lens; Eyepiece is not TEM lens; Eyepiece is not TEM lens.

questions.text: Which type of microscope is used to examine living cells outside the body (in tissue culture)?
questions.explanation: Phase contrast is the stated method for observing living unstained cells in tissue culture. Distinguishing alternatives: Generic light microscopy is less specific; Fluorescence requires an appropriate signal; TEM requires prepared thin specimens; SEM requires prepared surface specimens.

questions.text: Cultured cells are examined by........ microscope
questions.explanation: Phase contrast examines living unstained cultured cells.

questions.text: The maximum resolving power of the LM is:
questions.explanation: LM resolution is approximately0.2 micrometres.

questions.text: resolution power of electron microscope is:
questions.explanation: The course states TEM resolution around 0.1 nm, much finer than LM. Distinguishing alternatives: 0.2 nm is another instrument-dependent value but not the stated course value; 0.2 um is LM; 0.2 mm is macroscopic.

questions.text: Lenses of transmission E.M. are:
questions.explanation: Electron beams are focused by electromagnetic rather than glass lenses. Distinguishing alternatives: Glass lenses focus light; Ocular lenses are LM; TEM directs electrons rather than light.
options: ocular lens are one of them

questions.text: Magnification power of light microscope:
questions.explanation: Light-microscope total magnification equals objective magnification multiplied by ocular magnification.
options: condenser lens power x objective lens power
ocular lens power x objective lens power
ocular lens power x condenser lens power

questions.text: Supravital stain is:
questions.explanation: Supravital staining colors living cells outside the body. Distinguishing alternatives: Color shift is metachromasia; Enzyme localization is histochemistry; Living inside-body staining is vital.
options: a stained tissue component with a Color other than the color of dye
a suitable technique for enzyme demonstration in the cells.
staining of living cells outside the body.
staining of living cells inside the living body.

questions.text: Histochemical stain is:
questions.explanation: Histochemical reactions localize chemical constituents or enzyme activities in tissue. Distinguishing alternatives: Color shift is metachromasia; Outside-body living stain is supravital; Inside-body living stain is vital.
options: a stained tissue component with a Color other than the color of dye
a suitable technique for enzyme demonstration in the cells.
staining of living cells outside the body.
staining of living cells inside the living body.

questions.text: Example of supravital staining
questions.explanation: Janus-green mitochondria and reticulocyte vital dyes are supravital examples; injected trypan blue is vital.
options: Reticulocyte (immature RBCs) by crysle blus stain

questions.text: Vital staining
questions.explanation: Vital staining colors living cells within the organism. Distinguishing alternatives: Color shift is metachromasia; Enzyme localization is histochemistry; Outside-body staining is supravital.
options: a stained tissue component with a Color other than the color of dye
a suitable technique for enzyme demonstration in the cells.
staining of living cells outside the body.
staining of living cells inside the living body.

questions.text: E.M giving 3 dimensional view of cells outer surface
questions.explanation: SEM scans specimen surfaces to give a pseudo-three-dimensional surface view. Distinguishing alternatives: TEM examines internal thin sections; Phase contrast examines living unstained cells; Fluorescence shows labelled structures.

questions.text: mitochondria is stained supravitally with:
questions.explanation: Janus green B demonstrates mitochondria supravitally in fresh living cells outside the body.

questions.text: Resolution power of light microscope is :
questions.explanation: The designated course gives ordinary light-microscope resolution as approximately 0.2 micrometres.

questions.text: Good resolution of the microscope depends on the....
questions.explanation: Course assigns resolving power to objective lens.

questions.text: Fat is clearly demonstrated by which of the following stains:
questions.explanation: Sudan III demonstrates neutral lipids.

questions.text: Which of the following is characteristic for the freezing technique?
questions.explanation: Freezing preserves lipids and enzymes, is rapid and yields thicker difficult serial sections.
options: It is suitable for lipid demonstration.

questions.text: All of the following about transmission EM is true EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: TEM uses electron beam and electromagnetic lenses, not light wavelength.
options: The source of energy is a beam of electrons
The image is projected on either a fluorescent screen or a photographic film.
Depends on a wavelength of light
The condenser focuses the beam of electrons.

questions.text: The light microscope is characterized by:
questions.explanation: LM uses natural or electric visible light. Other statements describe TEM.
options: Having a resolution power equals to 0.1 nm
Using natural or electric light as a source of illumination
Its magnification reaches up to 120,000 times to observe fine details
Examining ultrathin sections are about 60-80 nm in thickness
Using heavy metal stains for examined tissues.

questions.text: Paraffin embedded sections for light microscopical examination are usually cut at the following thickness:
questions.explanation: Book routine5–8 micrometre sections fit5–10 micrometre alternative.

questions.text: Which of the following is considered a vital stain?
questions.explanation: Trypan blue is course vital dye.

questions.text: Histological stains used to:
questions.explanation: Staining distinguishes tissue constituents; other effects belong to preparation steps.
options: Preserve the tissue for long time.

questions.text: Which of the following is stained blue by H&E stain?
questions.explanation: Hematoxylin colours nuclear nucleic acids blue; eosin colours protein-rich structures pink.

questions.text: Focusing of electron beams on the specimen in the electron microscope is the function of:
questions.explanation: Condenser electromagnetic lens focuses electrons onto specimen.

questions.text: Which of the following connective tissue cells can be stained in vivo?
questions.explanation: Macrophages ingest trypan blue in living animal.

questions.text: Trypan blue and Sudan III stains can be used to detect which of the following types of cells RESPECTIVELY?
questions.explanation: Trypan blue demonstrates macrophages; Sudan III demonstrates adipocyte lipid.

questions.text: Which of the following histological methods is preferably used to demonstrate lipids?
questions.explanation: Freezing preserves lipid otherwise extracted during paraffin processing.

questions.text: Fixation of fresh tissue is essential to:
questions.explanation: Fixation preserves structure and prevents bacterial putrefaction before tissue processing.

questions.text: In dehydration of the tissue we use different grads of:
questions.explanation: Ascending alcohol concentrations progressively replace tissue water.

questions.text: The aim of dehydration is to:
questions.explanation: Dehydration removes water so a nonaqueous embedding medium can later infiltrate.

questions.text: Clearing is done by placing the tissues in:
questions.explanation: Xylol replaces alcohol and is miscible with paraffin.

questions.text: The most commonly used basic dye is:
questions.explanation: Hematoxylin is the routine nuclear/basic staining component of H&E.

questions.text: The most commonly used acidic dye is:
questions.explanation: Eosin is the routine acid dye staining protein-rich structures pink.

questions.text: Vital stain is:
questions.explanation: Vital staining labels living cells within the living body.
options: staining of dead tissue outside the body.
staining of a living cell inside the body.
staining of a living cell outside the body.
staining of a dead tissue inside the body.

questions.text: Advantages of paraffin sections:
questions.explanation: Paraffin sections are relatively easy to stain and can be thin and serial.
options: large pieces of tissues could be used.

questions.text: Advantages of celloidin sections:
questions.explanation: Avoidance of heating improves structural preservation in celloidin processing.
options: gives perfect preservations, as no heat is used.

questions.text: Paraffin sections are cut (for light microscope) at:
questions.explanation: The designated routine light-microscope paraffin section range is 5–8 micrometers.

questions.text: The purpose of the microscope is:
questions.explanation: Microscopes resolve details separated by distances below naked-eye resolution.

questions.text: The fixative has the following functions EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Fixation preserves and hardens tissue while generally increasing stain affinity.
options: Preserves the structure of the tissue.
Prevents the staining of the tissue.
Kills the bacteria in the tissue.

questions.text: One statement is NOT correct:
questions.explanation: Dehydration uses ascending alcohol concentrations; descending grades are used in rehydration before aqueous staining.
options: Dehydration occurs by descending grades of alcohol.
Xylol is a solvent used for clearing.
Embedding occurs in the hard paraffin.
The most common used fixative is formaldehyde.

questions.text: Paraffin technique has the following advantages EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Paraffin solvents remove lipids and heating impairs many enzyme activities, favoring frozen sections for these targets.
options: Suitable for staining lipid and enzymes.

questions.text: Following technique is suitable to stain the lipid and enzymes:
questions.explanation: Frozen processing avoids lipid-dissolving solvents and extensive heating.

questions.text: The most common staining system in the histology is:
questions.explanation: H&E provides complementary nuclear blue-purple and cytoplasmic pink staining.

questions.text: Which of the followings is suitable to examine the fat cells?
questions.explanation: Sudan black and Sudan III demonstrate lipids in appropriate sections.

questions.text: Periodic acid - Schiff reaction (PAS) is a suitable to stain:
questions.explanation: PAS detects carbohydrate-rich substances such as glycogen.

questions.text: One statement is NOT correct:
questions.explanation: Electron-microscope resolution is on the nanometer scale, not 0.2 millimeters.
options: Magnification power of the light microscope is 1500 times.
Resolution power of electron microscope is 0.2mm.
Resolution power of light microscope is 0.2 μm.
Magnification power of the electron microscope is up to 120,000 times.

questions.text: Three dimensional image for a cell can obtained by:
questions.explanation: SEM scans specimen surfaces to give a depth-like surface image, whereas TEM examines thin internal sections.

questions.text: Examples of Histochemical staining include the following except:
questions.explanation: PAS, enzyme reactions and lipid dyes are classified as histochemical demonstrations in the book; toluidine mast-cell staining is the metachromatic example.
options: Stain of lysosome by Acid phosphatase technique
Stain of fat cell by sudan III
Stain of mast cell by Toluidine blue

questions.text: resolution power of naked eye is :
questions.explanation: The designated naked-eye resolution is about 0.2 mm, much coarser than the 0.2 micrometer light microscope.

subjects.name: Histology
subjects.lectures: Cell organization and cytoskeleton overview, Plasma membrane structure and proteins, Glycocalyx and cell recognition, Membrane transport and endocytosis, Endosomes, Mitochondria, Rough and smooth endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi apparatus and secretion, Lysosomes and intracellular digestion, Peroxisomes and proteasomes, Ribosomes and protein synthesis, Microtubules and intracellular transport, Centrioles, cilia and flagella, Actin and intermediate filaments, Cytoplasmic inclusions and pigments, Nuclear envelope and pores, Chromatin and nuclear organization, Nucleolus and ribosome biogenesis, Cell cycle, renewal and division, Cell death and apoptosis, Chromosomes and chromosomal disorders

questions.text: On examining a cell of pancreatic acini by EM, you observe multiple zymogen granules in its cytoplasm. What is the organelle responsible for their formation?
questions.explanation: Golgi packages secretory proteins into zymogen granules.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of the constitutive pathway of protein secretion?
questions.explanation: Procollagen is continuously secreted for ECM; other alternatives are regulated hormonal or digestive secretions.

questions.text: In dealing with phagocytosed bacteria which of the following organelles are Primarily involved?
questions.explanation: Lysosomal hydrolases digest engulfed bacteria after delivery to the degradative pathway. Distinguishing alternatives: sER handles lipid metabolism; Peroxisomes oxidize metabolites; Endosomes sort and mature but lysosomal digestion is the primary bactericidal degradative role; rER synthesizes proteins.

questions.text: Hydrolytic enzymes are transferred from Golgi apparatus to which of the following organelles?
questions.explanation: Golgi-sorted hydrolases are delivered to late endosomes, which mature into lysosomes. Distinguishing alternatives: Phagosomes receive degradative machinery later; Secretory vesicles deliver exported proteins; Peroxisomes use oxidative enzymes; Proteasomes degrade ubiquitin-tagged proteins.

questions.text: Lysosomes resist being digested by their own hydrolytic enzymes due to presence of:
questions.explanation: Highly glycosylated luminal membrane proteins protect lysosome from its hydrolases.

questions.text: About secondary lysosome , all true except:
questions.explanation: Secondary degradative lysosomes result from fusion/maturation, rather than budding directly as secondary lysosomes from trans Golgi.
options: Arise from Trans face of Golgi
Formed by fusion of 1ry lysosome with endosome or autophagosome

questions.text: Which of the following terms best describes the remaining undigested particles after lysosomal digestion?
questions.explanation: Residual bodies retain material that remains undigested after lysosomal processing. Distinguishing alternatives: Phagosome begins particle uptake; Pinocytotic vesicles begin fluid uptake; Secretory vesicles export proteins; Autophagosomes enclose intracellular cargo before degradation.

questions.text: An 85-year-old woman with Alzheimer disease dies. Autopsy reveals hepatocytes with golden cytoplasmic granules. This aging pigments accumulates primarily within which of the following organelles?
questions.explanation: Age pigment accumulates in lysosomal residual bodies after incomplete digestion.

questions.text: Which of the following cellular processes describes the uptake of the extracellular fluids by the cell?
questions.explanation: Pinocytosis ingests extracellular fluid.

questions.text: Peroxisomes are characterized by....
questions.explanation: Peroxisomes are prominent membrane-bound oxidative organelles in liver and kidney. Distinguishing alternatives: They are membranous; Catalase rather than acid phosphatase is the marker; Oxidative rather than lysosomal hydrolases characterize them; They lack their own genome.
options: Being numerous in kidney and liver.

questions.text: Free ribosomes in the cell is responsible for formation of
questions.explanation: Free ribosomes make proteins used in cytosol and imported into nucleus, mitochondria or peroxisomes.

questions.text: Proteasomes differ from lysosomes in:
questions.explanation: Proteasomes recognize ubiquitin-tagged short-lived proteins and require ATP.

questions.text: Abnormal short lived proteins are degraded inside the cell by....
questions.explanation: Proteasomes remove abnormal and short-lived cytosolic proteins. Distinguishing alternatives: Lysosomes handle endocytic/autophagic material; Peroxisomes oxidize metabolites; Endosomes sort cargo; Phagosomes contain ingested particles.

questions.text: Intermediate filaments are:
questions.explanation: Intermediate filaments support cytoplasm, and lamins form the nuclear lamina. Distinguishing alternatives: They do not directly generate contraction; Their diameter is about 10 nm; Composition varies by cell type; Tubulin forms microtubules.

questions.text: All of the following are intermediate filaments, EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Actin thin filaments and myosin thick filaments differ from intermediate-filament families. Distinguishing alternatives: Keratin is intermediate; Neurofilaments are intermediate; Glial filaments are intermediate; Lamins are intermediate.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a function of microtubules?
questions.explanation: Microvilli have actin cores rather than microtubules. Distinguishing alternatives: Cilia have microtubules; Microtubules support transport; Spindle microtubules move chromosomes; Microtubules support cell shape.
options: They form structural component of cilia.
They facilitate intracellular transport of organelles.
They are involved in chromosomal movement during mitosis.
They form structural core of microvilli.

questions.text: Assembly of microtubules is initiated near the...
questions.explanation: Centrosomal region around centrioles initiates microtubule assembly.

questions.text: Which of the following statements truly describes the microtubules?
questions.explanation: A typical microtubule wall contains 13 longitudinal protofilaments of tubulin. Distinguishing alternatives: Microtubules have dynamic lengths; The stated assembly pattern is not the usual plus-end emphasis; Nucleolar organizer forms rRNA rather than microtubules.
options: Their tublin subunits are added at its minus end.
They are assembled in the nucleolar organizer region

questions.text: Which of the following intermediate filaments are associated with the inner nuclear envelope?
questions.explanation: Lamins form intermediate filaments of the nuclear lamina beneath the inner nuclear membrane. Distinguishing alternatives: Desmin is muscle intermediate filament; Vimentin is cytoplasmic mesenchymal intermediate filament; Tubulin is microtubule protein; Actin is microfilament protein.

questions.text: Which of the following proteins contributes to the structural matrix that anchors chromatin to the nuclear membrane during interphase of the cell cycle?
questions.explanation: Nuclear lamins form structural lamina attaching chromatin to inner nuclear membrane.

questions.text: The outer nuclear envelope is continuous with...........
questions.explanation: The outer nuclear membrane is continuous with rough ER and bears ribosomes. Distinguishing alternatives: sER lacks the defining ribosomes; Centrioles are nonmembranous; Lysosomes are separate vesicles; Golgi is a separate membrane system.

questions.text: Which of the following structures can be seen passing through nuclear pore complex?
questions.explanation: Ribosomal subunits are exported through nuclear pore complexes. Distinguishing alternatives: Whole microtubules are not pore cargo; ER membranes do not traverse pores; rRNA genes remain chromosomal; DNA loops remain nuclear.

questions.text: Each of the following statement concerning the nuclear envelop is true EXCEPT;
questions.explanation: The two membranes differ: outer is ribosome-studded, inner is lamina/chromatin-associated. Distinguishing alternatives: Nuclear pores are present; Envelope separates nucleus/cytoplasm; Envelope disassembles during mitotic prophase.
options: It consists of two symmetrical unit membrane
It is a boundary between the nucleus and cytoplasm.

questions.text: Each of the following statements concerning the nucleoleus is true EXCEPT;
questions.explanation: Nucleolus has distinct light and dense fibrillar/granular regions rather than homogeneous granules. Distinguishing alternatives: Organizer contains DNA loops; Nucleolus produces rRNA; Multiple nucleoli can occur.
options: It has a homogenous granular appearance on EM.
It is responsible for formation of r RNA.
The nucleus may contain more than one nucleoleus.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is TRUE concerning the nucleolus?
questions.explanation: Protein-synthesizing cells have prominent nucleoli producing ribosomal components. Distinguishing alternatives: Nucleolus lacks a limiting membrane; Fibrosa contains newly formed rRNA rather than mature subunits; rRNA genes are in organizer regions; Nucleolus disappears during division and reappears afterward.
options: It is prominent in protein secreting cells.
Its pars fibrosa contains mature form of ribosomal subunits.
Ribosomal RNA genes are present in its pars granulosa.

questions.text: Ribosomal RNA is synthesized by:
questions.explanation: rRNA is transcribed in the nucleolus. Distinguishing alternatives: sER makes lipids; rER translates proteins; Golgi modifies proteins; Secretory vesicles package products.

questions.text: By using E/M, the nucleolus ....
questions.explanation: Pars fibrosa contains newly formed rRNA strands. Distinguishing alternatives: Basophilic masses describes LM, not EM; Nucleolus is nonmembranous; Maturing subunits occur in granulosa.
options: is seen as one or more basophilic masses.
is surrounded by two unit membranes.
Shows maturing ribosomal subunits in its pars fibrosa
shows rRNA strands in pars fibrosa

questions.text: Nucleolar organizer region contains which of the following?
questions.explanation: Nucleolar organizer regions contain ribosomal DNA genes directing rRNA formation. Distinguishing alternatives: Lamina supports nuclear envelope; New subunits are granulosa material; RNA is the product, not organizer genes; Mature subunits are not the organizer genes.

questions.text: which of the following terminology best describes the darkly stained shrunken nucleus?
questions.explanation: Pyknosis is nuclear shrinkage with intense staining.

questions.text: Which of the following increases with age?
questions.explanation: Lipofuscin wear-and-tear granules accumulate with age.

questions.text: PAS stained section of the liver shows cells with abundant pink granules in the cytoplasm. Which of the following terms best describes these granules?
questions.explanation: PAS-positive hepatic glycogen is stored material classified as a cytoplasmic inclusion. Distinguishing alternatives: Fragments is nonspecific; Vesicles are membrane compartments; Vacuoles are spaces/compartments; Organelles perform living-cell functions.

questions.text: Which of the following structures can identify a TEM of adrenal cortex?
questions.explanation: Steroid-synthesizing adrenal cortical cells combine extensive sER with tubular mitochondrial cristae.

questions.text: What is the site of ATP synthase (phosphorylation enzymes)?
questions.explanation: ATP synthase resides in the inner mitochondrial membrane and its cristae. Distinguishing alternatives: Matrix houses citric-cycle enzymes; Outer membrane is not the ATP-synthase location; Peroxisomes do not generate ATP this way.

questions.text: Of the following cell type ,which would contain mitochondria in the apical part o the cell.
questions.explanation: Mitochondria gather where ATP demand is high, including apical ciliary motion. Distinguishing alternatives: Smooth muscle has variable mitochondrial placement; Skeletal muscle mitochondria follow contractile energy demand; Steroid cells have abundant mitochondria but apical cilia are not their feature.

questions.text: Using transmission electron microscope, mitochondria are....
questions.explanation: Mitochondria have outer and inner membranes.
options: Formed of series of flattened cisternae.
Continuous with the outer nuclear envelope

questions.text: Molecular structure of cell membrane include the following except:
questions.explanation: Ribophorins are rough-ER associated proteins, not one of the usual plasma-membrane molecular components.

questions.text: Unit membrane means:
questions.explanation: Unit membrane is the trilaminar electron-microscopic appearance of a membrane. Distinguishing alternatives: A lipid layer alone is not the EM unit-membrane term; One dense line omits three layers; LM cannot resolve the unit membrane.
options: One electron dense line with its associated cell coat.
Cell boundaries as seen by L.M.

questions.text: About Cholesterol molecules in cell membrane all true except:
questions.explanation: Cholesterol sits among phospholipids in both membrane leaflets rather than in the carbohydrate glycocalyx.
options: Present in the inner & outer phospholipid layers.
Its function is stabilization of the cell membrane.
Keep the phospholipid molecules packed close together.

questions.text: The following are functions of cell coat except:
questions.explanation: Glycocalyx supports adhesion, recognition and receptor interactions, rather than intracellular carbohydrate metabolism.

questions.text: About cell membrane, the following is true except:
questions.explanation: The plasma-membrane bilayer is below conventional LM resolving power. Distinguishing alternatives: Trilaminar EM appearance is true; Nanometre thickness is true; Leaflets differ in lipid/protein composition.
options: Appears as Trilaminar appearance by E.M.
Seen by L.M. in all cells.
Its outer & inner layers include different types of phospholipids & proteins.

questions.text: About membrane proteins, the following is true except:
questions.explanation: Peripheral proteins bind surfaces rather than being embedded in the hydrophobic bilayer. Distinguishing alternatives: Integral/peripheral classes are supported; Protein mass contribution is supported; Peripheral proteins support cytoskeleton.
options: Has 2 main types, integral & peripheral membrane proteins.
Proteins are a major molecular constituent of the cell membrane (about 50%) [according to weight]
Peripheral membrane proteins are embedded within the lipids bilayer.
Peripheral membrane protein function as support for the cytoskeleton.

questions.text: Integral membrane proteins:
questions.explanation: Integral transmembrane proteins can form ion channels through the bilayer. Distinguishing alternatives: Loosely surface-bound describes peripheral proteins; Integral proteins are not universally excluded from inner leaflet; Cholesterol is the stated major stabilizing factor.
options: Are loosely attached to the outer part of phospholipid bilayer.
Are not attached to the inner part of phospholipid bilayer.
Are the main cause for stability of the membrane.

questions.text: Intrinsic or integral membrane proteins, all true except:
questions.explanation: Integral proteins can span the membrane or occupy either leaflet; they are not confined to the inner leaflet.
options: May act as ion channels or ion pumps
Each molecule has a non-polar hydrophobic region and a polar hydrophilic region.
Present in the inner lipid layer only

questions.text: Extrinsic or peripheral membrane proteins, all true except:
questions.explanation: The course assigns extracellular receptor and channel roles to integral proteins and cytoskeletal support to peripheral proteins.
options: These are loosely bound to both inner and outer surfaces of the cell membrane
Its surface lack the non-polar portion

questions.text: integral membrane proteins are;
questions.explanation: Integral proteins include transmembrane proteins embedded across the lipid bilayer. Distinguishing alternatives: Integral proteins can associate with outer leaflet; Membrane stability is not their defining main function; Integral proteins can associate with inner leaflet.
options: not attached to the outer leaflets.
Main function in the stability of the membrane.
not attached to the inner leaflets

questions.text: The plasma membrane has the following functions EXCEPT;
questions.explanation: Protein synthesis occurs on ribosomes rather than being the primary role of plasma membrane. Distinguishing alternatives: Selective barrier is true; Cell adhesion is true; Hormone receptor interactions are true.
options: It is the primary site of protein biosynthesis
It is a cell adhesion interface
It is a site for hormone receptors.

questions.text: The following statements are true about integral protein EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Integral proteins are embedded in the lipid bilayer; loose surface binding defines peripheral proteins.
options: Each molecule has hydrophilic & hydrophobic region.
It is loosely bound to the surface of lipid bilayer.
It may extend from one side of the cell membrane to the other side

questions.text: About cell coat [glycocalyx], all true except:
questions.explanation: Cell coat consists of carbohydrate moieties on exposed glycoproteins and glycolipids. Distinguishing alternatives: Outward glycolipids contribute; Exposed glycoproteins contribute; Cell recognition/adhesion is supported.
options: Some of the outward-facing lipid molecules forming glycolipids.
Cholesterol is a main constituent of the cell coat.
Most of the outward-facing proteins constituting glycoproteins.
Has a key role in cell recognition and cell adhesion.

questions.text: About cell coat, all of the following statements are correct EXCEPT;
questions.explanation: Cholesterol is a bilayer lipid rather than a glycocalyx constituent. Distinguishing alternatives: Coat is external; Carbohydrates give PAS positivity; Coat mediates recognition.
options: it is located on the outer surface of the membrane.
it is involved in cell to cell recognition.

questions.text: Differences between the outer and inner aspects of the cell membrane, include the following except:
questions.explanation: Cholesterol is present in both lipid leaflets while glycocalyx projects extracellularly. Distinguishing alternatives: External coat/receptor domains are supported; Lipid leaflet asymmetry is supported; Protein asymmetry is supported.
options: Cell coat & receptors are present on the outer surface only.
Different lipid components in both layers.
Different protein components in both layers.
Cholesterol is present in the outer layer only

questions.text: Mitochondria can be demonstrated with L.M. by the following except:
questions.explanation: Mitochondria can be demonstrated with iron hematoxylin or supravital Janus green, unlike injected trypan-blue macrophage staining.
options: Supravital staining with Janus Green B.

questions.text: Mitochondrial matrix contains the following except:
questions.explanation: Oxidative-phosphorylation machinery resides in the inner membrane/cristae rather than mitochondrial matrix.

questions.text: Each of the following statements concerning mitochondria is true EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Catalase is the characteristic peroxisomal enzyme rather than the mitochondrial respiratory enzyme. Distinguishing alternatives: Respiratory enzymes are mitochondrial; Inner membrane has cristae; Outer membrane is smooth.
options: they contain enzymes for electron transport.(respiration)

questions.text: Mitochondria:
questions.explanation: Mitochondria move/divide, generate ATP at the inner membrane and can support brown-fat thermogenesis.
options: Cristae are carrying ATP synthetase which produce ATP.
In some cells Can generate heat.

questions.text: The following are functions of sER except:
questions.explanation: sER handles lipid metabolism, detoxification and calcium regulation; ribosomal protein synthesis is associated with rER/free ribosomes.

questions.text: By EM, smooth endoplasmic reticulum appears:
questions.explanation: sER is a smooth branching/anastomosing tubular membrane network. Distinguishing alternatives: Parallel cisternae characterize rER; Dense-core vesicles are other compartments; Nuclear continuity chiefly identifies outer envelope/rER; Protein-secretory richness characterizes rER.

questions.text: Steroid forming cells are characterized by the following except:
questions.explanation: Steroid-secreting cells have extensive sER, lipid droplets and tubular mitochondrial cristae rather than predominant rER.
options: Contain numerous mitochondria with tubular Cristae.

questions.text: Protein secreting cells are rich in:
questions.explanation: Protein-secretory cells need both rER for synthesis and Golgi for processing/packaging. Distinguishing alternatives: rER is abundant; Golgi is abundant; Neither is false.

questions.text: About rER all is true except:
questions.explanation: rER regions create localized basophilia; diffuse basophilia is associated with free ribosomes. Distinguishing alternatives: rER continuity with sER/envelope is true; Ribosome-studded cisternae are true; Transfer vesicles carry rER products.
options: connected with the smooth ER and the outer nuclear membrane.
Interconnected flattened parallel cisternae studded with ribosomes
Result in diffuse basophilia seen with L.M.
proteins are transferred to the Golgi apparatus via the transfer vesicles

questions.text: The main organelle responsible for protein synthesis is:
questions.explanation: Among the options, rough ER supplies attached ribosomes for synthesis of secretory and membrane proteins.

questions.text: About Golgi complex, all are true except:
questions.explanation: Golgi is prominent in protein-secretory cells; steroid synthesis chiefly emphasizes sER. Distinguishing alternatives: Vesicular traffic links Golgi processing compartments; Silver staining is supported; Membrane-protein distribution is supported.
options: Its saccules are interconnected through transfere vesicles.
So numerous in steroid forming cells.

questions.text: an example of multinucleated cells:

its formation initiated near centrioles & basal body
cannot be used in intracellular transport
are formed of heterogenous group of proteins

questions.text: in the following , which structure is not involved of cytoskeleton formation:
questions.explanation: The course cytoskeleton consists of microtubules, thin actin and intermediate filaments; thick myosin is classified separately as contractile filament.

questions.text: Regarding the peripheral protein of the cell membrane, one of the following statement is true:
questions.explanation: Peripheral proteins associate loosely with membrane surfaces rather than crossing the hydrophobic core.
options: Are deeply embedded in lipid bilayer
Are loosly associated with lipid bilayer
Are single or multi pass in lipid bilayer
Are transmembrane proteins in lipid bilayer

questions.text: Peroxisomes:
questions.explanation: Peroxisomes are membrane-bound oxidative organelles containing catalase.

questions.text: About cytoskeleton, all are true EXCEPT:

questions.explanation: Membrane proteins provide channels/receptors; membrane fluidity depends principally on lipid organization and is not uniformly increased by proteins.

questions.text: The organelle considered with protein synthesis:
questions.explanation: Ribosomes translate mRNA into protein; smooth ER lacks ribosomes and specializes in lipid metabolism.

questions.text: About cytoskeletal system, all are true EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The course cytoskeleton is microtubules, actin/thin and intermediate filaments; thick filaments are a separate contractile class.
options: Consists of thin, intermediate & thick filament

questions.text: The organelle protects the cells from hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) cellular damage:
questions.explanation: Peroxisomal catalase breaks down hydrogen peroxide and prevents its accumulation.

questions.text: Detoxification in the cells is formed by:
questions.explanation: sER contains detoxification systems; peroxisomal oxidative detoxification is an additional pathway but is not among these options.

questions.text: The free ribosomes are responsible for synthesize of:
questions.explanation: Free ribosomes synthesize intracellular proteins rather than the secretory protein pathway.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a membranous organelle?
questions.explanation: Ribosomes are non-membranous RNA/protein particles.

questions.text: The process by which the cell membrane engulfs a solid particle is called:
questions.explanation: Phagocytosis engulfs solid particles into phagosomes.

questions.text: All the following is considered as cytoskeleton EXCEPT one:
questions.explanation: Ribosomes perform translation and are not structural cytoskeleton components.

questions.text: The plasma membrane characterized by the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Membrane lipids include phospholipids plus cholesterol and glycolipids, so phospholipid-only is incorrect.
options: By EM appear as trilaminar membrane
Its lipid component formed of phospholipid only

questions.text: Functions of Golgi complex include:
questions.explanation: Golgi processes, concentrates and packages secretory protein, including carbohydrate modification.

questions.text: The cell membrane is composed of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Carbohydrate, protein and lipid are general membrane constituents; antibodies are not a universal basic constituent, although membrane immunoglobulin exists in specialized B cells.

questions.text: All of the following are exoganous pigments EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Lipofuscin is an endogenous wear-and-tear pigment accumulating from incompletely digested intracellular material.
options: Lipofuscin pigments as in nerve cells

questions.text: The cell active in protein synthesis have prominent:
questions.explanation: Active protein synthesis involves ribosomes, rER for secretory proteins and prominent rRNA-producing nucleolus.

questions.text: The basophilia in the cytoplasm is due to presence of:
questions.explanation: Ribosomal RNA, free or rER-bound, gives cytoplasm affinity for basic dyes.

questions.text: Apoptosis:
questions.explanation: Apoptosis is regulated programmed cell death with cellular/nuclear condensation and fragmentation.
options: Starts by decrease in the size of the cell

questions.text: One of the following is a non membranous organelles :
questions.explanation: Ribosomes have no limiting membrane. Distinguishing alternatives: Mito membrane; Golgi membrane; rER membrane; sER membrane.

questions.text: The cell organelle responsible for synthesis of lipids is:
questions.explanation: Smooth ER synthesizes intracellular lipids and cholesterol derivatives.

questions.text: Functions of centerioles include:
questions.explanation: Centrioles organize microtubules for mitotic spindle and basal bodies; the organized microtubule system also supports vesicular transport.

questions.text: Cells rich in mictochondria:
questions.explanation: Liver metabolism, striated-muscle contraction and proximal-tubule transport all demand substantial ATP and abundant mitochondria.

questions.text: In cell division, all is true EXCEPT :
questions.explanation: Homologues pair before segregation and move apart at anaphaseI; they are not retained as paired chromosomes at that stage.
options: In anaphase I, chromosomes arranged in pairs

questions.text: All is true about chromosomes, EXCEPT :
questions.explanation: Neurons retain sex chromosomes just as other nucleated somatic cells; mature red blood corpuscles are the notable anucleate exception.
options: Nerve cells has no sex chromosomes
Somatic cells have 23 pairs of chromosomes

questions.text: The nucleolus consists of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Nucleolus is nonmembranous and contains organizer, fibrous and granular regions.

questions.text: Concerning chromatin, the following is true :
questions.explanation: Vesicular nuclei contain more transcriptionally active euchromatin.
options: Euchromatin is more coiled and active
Cells with vesicular nuclei are more active than those of condenced nuclei
Heterochromatin is more in active cells

questions.text: Each somatic (Body) cells usually contains :
questions.explanation: Ordinary human somatic cells are diploid; specialized exceptions do not change usually.

questions.text: Genetic information present in the nucleus is carried by compact of chromatin threads known as :
questions.explanation: Chromosomes are compacted chromatin carrying genetic information.

questions.text: Barr body represents :
questions.explanation: Barr body is an inactivated X chromosome.

questions.text: Chromosomal constitution of an individual is known as :
questions.explanation: Karyotype describes chromosome constitution.

questions.text: DNA is replicated during :
questions.explanation: S phase lies within interphase.

questions.text: The phase of mitosis during which we stop cell division for karyotyping is :
questions.explanation: Colchicine arrests spindle-dependent mitosis with condensed metaphase chromosomes suitable for karyotyping.

questions.text: Human chromosome at metaphase consists of :
questions.explanation: After S phase each metaphase chromosome has two sister chromatids joined at its centromere.

questions.text: During G2 phase, the following occurs EXCEPT :
questions.explanation: Book explicitly places centriole duplication in S phase, making it the G2 exception.

questions.text: All are correct as regards DNA EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Nuclear DNA is ordinarily a double-stranded helix with deoxyribose phosphate backbone and heritable protein coding information.
options: Backbone is formed of suger 2-deoxy D-ribose & phosphoric
Genes on DNA are transferred during division
Formed of a single strand only

questions.text: The smallest structural unit of chromatin is called
questions.explanation: Nucleosome is chromatin basic structural unit.

questions.text: Sex chromatin (Barr body) :
questions.explanation: Sex chromatin represents inactive X; the given blood and epithelial frequency claims are reversed relative to classic smear teaching.
options: Is present in 60 % of female blood leukocytes
Is present in 3-5% of female epithelial cells
Represents inactive X chromosome in female cell nuclei

questions.text: Chromatin is composed mainly of :
questions.explanation: Chromatin is DNA associated with histone proteins; nucleosomes organize DNA around histone cores.
options: Coiled strands of DNA bound to basic proteins (histones)
Coiled strands of RNA bound to basic proteins (histones)
Coiled strands of DNA and RNA bound to ribose sugar

questions.text: About nuclear pore complex, all are true except:
questions.explanation: Nuclear pore complexes guard envelope transport; nucleolus has no membrane separating it from chromatin.
options: Cylindrical protein complex guarding the nuclear pores.
Filaments extend from outer cytoplasmic ring into cytoplasm.
Filaments extend from inner nuclear ring to form a BASKET.

questions.text: About nuclear envelope, all are true except:
questions.explanation: Perinuclear space lies between membranes and continues with ER lumen rather than cytosolic protein compartment.
options: Formed of 2 membranes enclosing a perinuclear space.
Outer membrane is continuous with rER.
Inner membrane is supported by nuclear lamina.

questions.text: The following appear electron dense with EM except:
questions.explanation: Euchromatin is dispersed and electron lucent; heterochromatin glycogen and ribosomes are dense.

questions.text: About nucleolus , the following is true except:
questions.explanation: Fibrous nucleolar region contains newly synthesized rRNA; DNA genes reside in organizer regions.
options: Have 3 types of electron dense areas as seen by E.M.
DNA organizer appear as Pale electron dense area

questions.text: Nuclear signs of cell death include the following except:
questions.explanation: Karyotyping analyzes chromosomes; pyknosis fragmentation and dissolution are death changes.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is TRUE about nuclear lamina?
questions.explanation: Intermediate-filament nuclear lamina supports inner nuclear membrane.
options: It can be stained by anti-keratin
It supports the inner nuclear membrane
It anchors the nucleolus associated chromatin to the nucleolus.

questions.text: By using E/M, the nucleolus ....
questions.explanation: Organizer contains genes for ribosomal RNA. Basophilic masses are LM description, and mature subunits occupy granular region.
options: is seen as one or more basophilic masses.
is surrounded by two unit membranes.
Shows maturing ribosomal subunits in its pars fibrosa.
genes for ribosomal RNA are present in nucleolus organiser

questions.text: Which of the following statements concerning chromatin is TRUE?
questions.explanation: Nucleosomes are chromatin structural units; extended euchromatin is active and electron lucent.
options: Nucleosomes constitutes its basic structural unit.
Extended chromatin can be seen by light microscope.

questions.text: A child 3 years old presented to the pediatric clinic with limited growth, lack of body fat and muscles, hair loss including eye lashes and eye brows, with wrinkled shrunken face, visible veins and thin skin. Genetic investigations reveal mutations in the gene coding for lamin A. The condition is diagnosed as Progeria (premature aging). Which of the following structures are expected to be affected in such a case?
questions.explanation: Lamin A mutation disrupts nuclear lamina/envelope in progeria.

questions.text: Which of the following organelles is responsible for the basophilia of the cytoplasm of plasma cells using hematoxylin and eosin stains?
questions.explanation: Abundant rER ribosomal RNA causes basophilic plasma-cell cytoplasm.

questions.text: Trilaminar appearance seen in E/M photos is due to:
questions.explanation: Book attributes dense membrane layers to osmium on hydrophilic heads.
options: An artifact during staining of the cell membrane
Deposition of osmium on hydrophobic aspects of the cell membrane
Adherent junction between adjacent cell membranes
Deposition of osmium on hydrophilic aspects of cell membrane
Tight junction between two cell membranes

questions.text: Channels and carriers for passive and active transport are facilitated by:
questions.explanation: Integral transmembrane proteins form channels and carriers.

questions.text: The cell components responsible for the movable mosaic within the fluid lipid bilayer:
questions.explanation: Proteins make the membrane mosaic within fluid lipid bilayer.

questions.text: Phagosome is defined as:
questions.explanation: Phagosome encloses ingested solid material.
options: An Extruded vesicle throughout the cell.

questions.text: Organelles involved in lipid synthesis are:
questions.explanation: sER and peroxisomes participate in lipid metabolism/synthesis.

questions.text: On examination of a cell by E/M, rER appears as:
questions.explanation: rER consists of interconnected flattened cisternae with ribosomes.

questions.text: What is the membranous vesicle which primarily fuses with the coated vesicle?
questions.explanation: Coated endocytic vesicles fuse with early endosomes.

questions.text: Impairment of liver, kidney and nervous tissue is diagnosed as Zellweger syndrome. Lab investigation reveals deficiency in catalase enzymes. What organelle is responsible for this condition?
questions.explanation: Zellweger is peroxisome deficiency with liver kidney neurological injury and catalase deficit.

questions.text: Which of the following organelles are responsible for separating the receptors and ligands of the coated vesicles?
questions.explanation: Early endosome pH6 separates ligands and receptors.

questions.text: EM photo of the mitochondria showed the cristae in a tubular form. This photo is for which of the following cells.
questions.explanation: Tubular cristae characterize steroid-producing adrenal cortical cells; no supplied image needed to answer described finding.

questions.text: Secretory vesicles originate as budding from the......
questions.explanation: Secretory vesicles bud from trans Golgi.

questions.text: Light microscopic examination of a section of the stomach reveals multiple chief cells with apical zymogen granules. Electron microscopic examination of these "protein synthesizing" cells show an abundance of which of the following organelles?
questions.explanation: Chief cells synthesize secretory proteins on extensive rER.

questions.text: A hematoxylin and eosin stained section shows a cell with large vacuolated cytoplasm, thin rim of cytoplasm and a flattened peripheral nucleus. Which of the following terms best describes the large vacuolated area in such a signet-ring appearing cell?
questions.explanation: Signet-ring adipocyte space is a lipid inclusion dissolved by routine processing.

questions.text: The newly formed ribosomes are present in...
questions.explanation: Maturing newly formed ribosomal subunits occupy pars granulosa.

questions.text: steroid secreting cells have NUMEROUS...
questions.explanation: Steroid cells contain abundant sER.

questions.text: Stability of the cell membrane is a function of...
questions.explanation: Book cholesterol stabilizes membrane bilayer.

questions.text: The exchange of 8 nm histone protein through the nuclear pore complex is done by...
questions.explanation: Course requires active transport for large cargo through pore; an8nm histone protein is above small diffusible cargo.

questions.text: Which of the following is characterized by structural instability?
questions.explanation: Microtubules undergo assembly/disassembly; axonemal cilia/flagella and intermediate filaments are comparatively stable.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about heterochromatin is TRUE?
questions.explanation: Heterochromatin contains transcriptionally inactive genes in course terminology.
options: By LM appears as acidophilic granules
It is formed of uncoiled chromatin threads
By EM, it is present only surrounding the nucleolus

questions.text: The organelles which are involved in calcium regulation are............
questions.explanation: Mitochondria and sER regulate/store calcium.

questions.text: Which of the following organelles has its own DNA?
questions.explanation: Mitochondrial matrix contains its own DNA.

questions.text: Light microscopic examination of cardiac muscle fibers reveals brown pigments. These pigment might be..................
questions.explanation: Brown wear-and-tear pigment in cardiac cells is lipofuscin.

questions.text: Proteins synthesized by free ribosomes are directed to which of the following?
questions.explanation: Free ribosomes make proteins imported to peroxisomes; other listed destinations use bound secretory pathway.

questions.text: Centrosome is ...

questions.explanation: Organizer is DNA loops carrying rRNA genes.

questions.explanation: Nucleolus has rRNA-gene organizer region.
options: is seen as one or more basophilic masses.
is surrounded by two unit membranes.
Shows maturing ribosomal subunits in its pars fibrosa.

questions.explanation: Intermediate filaments provide intracellular cytoskeletal support.
options: Can be detected by scanning electron microscope.
Forms mitotic spindle during cell division.
Motor proteins are attached to them.
Shares in the cytoskeleton of the cell

questions.explanation: Vimentin labels mesenchymal vascular elements rather than epithelial keratin or nuclear lamins.
options: Basal plasma membrane of the cells.

questions.text: Which of the following are considered cytoplasmic inclusions?
questions.explanation: Hemosiderin is stored endogenous pigment inclusion; secretory granules are membrane-bound organelles in course taxonomy.

questions.text: Euchromatin is characterized by which of the following?

It can be demonstrated by L/M.

It is present in the basal part of the cell.
It has two central singlet of microfilaments.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is TRUE about mitochondria?

options: Are formed of series of flattened cisternae.
Are surrounded by a single membrane.
Can be visualized by H&E stain.

It is present in the basal part of the cell.

questions.explanation: Peroxisomes contain oxidative enzymes, particularly oxidases/catalase.

options: Is present in the basal part of the cell.
Has two central singlet of microfilaments.

questions.explanation: Golgi supplies membrane vesicles and participates in membrane renewal.

Visible with the LM with Hematoxylin and Eosin stain.
The site of packaging of secretory products of the cell.

Channel for fat soluble substance to pass through.

questions.explanation: Pinocytosis internalizes fluid droplets. Distinguishing alternatives: Solid phagocytosis; Bacteria phagocytosis; Foreign solid phagocytosis; Dead cells phagocytosis.

Plays a role in cell adhesion & recognition.

Its enzymes are synthesized by attached polysomes.

questions.explanation: Ribosomal RNA binds hematoxylin. Distinguishing alternatives: sER not; Golgi negative; Lysosome not characteristic; Membrane not characteristic.

questions.text: Ribosomes are:
questions.explanation: Ribosomes are nonmembranous protein-synthesis organelles. Distinguishing alternatives: No membrane; Not pigment; Not stored food; Not chromatin.

questions.text: The organelle responsible for synthesis of secreted proteins is:
questions.explanation: Attached ribosomes synthesize proteins entering secretory pathway. Distinguishing alternatives: Mito internal proteins; Lysosome digests; sER lacks ribosomes; Free cytosolic proteins.

questions.text: One is regarded as an endogenous pigment:

questions.text: Which of the following share in cell division:
questions.explanation: Centrioles contribute to spindle organization. Distinguishing alternatives: Keratin epithelial IF; Vimentin IF; Glial IF; Desmin muscle IF.

questions.text: Glycogen granules are stained with:
questions.explanation: Best carmine is a glycogen stain. Distinguishing alternatives: Osmium lipid; Silver other; Sudan lipid; Janus mitochondria.

questions.text: The outer layer of the nuclear envelope:
questions.explanation: Outer nuclear membrane bears ribosomes and is granular. Distinguishing alternatives: Smooth wrong; Cristae mito; Fibrillar wrong; Not clathrin coat.

questions.explanation: Nuclear pore complex has octagonal symmetry. Distinguishing alternatives: Not triangular; Membranes fuse; RNA usually exported; Extensions both sides.

Concerned with import of RNA to the nucleus.
Nucleoporin filaments extend only into the cytoplasm.

questions.text: Pars amorpha of the nucleolus:

Are formed of two subunits of equal size.
Are concerned with beta oxidation of long chain fatty acid.

questions.text: Duplication of the centrioles occurs at:

questions.text: Which description is correct for karyorrhexis?

The nuclei and chromatin are fragmented by DNA ligase enzyme.
The nuclei and chromatin are fragmented by endonuclease enzyme.

questions.text: Colchicine is a chemical that stops chromatids from separating during mitosis at:
questions.explanation: Colchicine disrupts spindle microtubules and arrests cells at metaphase before chromatid segregation.

questions.text: In karyotyping the chromosomes are obtained in:
questions.explanation: Condensed metaphase chromosomes are used for conventional karyotyping. Distinguishing alternatives: Not preferred; Already separated; Decondensing; Uncondensed.

May be due to multiple X syndrome.

questions.text: Cilia grow from the basal bodies & remain attached to it.
