questions.text: Immotile cilia syndrome (respiratory tract infection + infertility) is due to defect in:
questions.explanation: Dynein-arm defects impair axonemal sliding, disrupting airway clearance and sperm motility.

questions.text: Axoneme (shaft ) of Cilia contain:
questions.explanation: Nine doublets plus two central singlets yield 20 microtubules, unlike the 27 of a basal body.

questions.text: Organelle receiving lytic enzymes from Golgi apparatus is:
questions.explanation: Late endosomes receive Golgi-derived lysosomal enzymes and mature toward the degradative lysosomal compartment.

questions.text: In ciliated cells, mitochondria are situated in:
questions.explanation: Ciliated cells concentrate mitochondria near apical cilia to support beating energy demand.
options: In the lateral region of cytoplasm

questions.text: Colchicine is used as antimitotic drug because
questions.explanation: Colchicine binds tubulin and inhibits microtubule assembly, preventing formation of a functional mitotic spindle.
options: It prevents microtubule polymerization (prevent mitotic spindle formation)

questions.text: Alpha granules of Glycogen are present in
questions.explanation: Hepatocytes characteristically contain rosette-like alpha aggregates; muscle glycogen predominantly uses smaller beta particles.

questions.text: Lipid droplets are prominent in the following cells except:
questions.explanation: Adipocytes and steroid-forming cells have prominent lipid stores; ordinary muscle is not the characteristic lipid-droplet-dominated cell.

questions.text: Mitochondrial matrix in E.M show electron dense bodies of:
questions.explanation: Electron-dense matrix granules bind calcium; respiratory enzymes are membrane-associated.

questions.text: The more acidophilic cytoplasm contain numerous:
questions.explanation: Mitochondrial proteins contribute eosinophilic cytoplasmic staining, whereas ribosomal RNA causes basophilia.

questions.text: spotty basophilia appear in:
questions.explanation: Neuronal Nissl substance consists of grouped rough ER and ribosomes producing spotty basophilia.

questions.text: Mitochondria with tubular crista are present in:
questions.explanation: Steroid-producing adrenal cortical cells characteristically have tubular or vesicular mitochondrial cristae, unlike the lamellar cristae of many other cells.

questions.text: By L.M. the rER shows:
questions.explanation: Rough ER forms localized basophilic regions from attached ribosomal RNA; neuronal arrangements can produce Nissl patches.

questions.text: In centriole tubule A of its triblets is formed of:
questions.explanation: The complete A tubule has 13 protofilaments; incomplete B and C share its wall.

subjects.name: Histology
subjects.lectures: General epithelial features and renewal, Simple and pseudostratified epithelium, Stratified squamous and columnar epithelium, Transitional epithelium, Gland classification and architecture, Serous, mucous and goblet cells, Modes of glandular secretion, Neuroepithelium and myoepithelium, Apical specializations, Cell junctions, Basement membrane and basal specializations

questions.text: Change of type of epithelium into another type is called :
questions.explanation: Metaplasia is replacement of one differentiated epithelial type by another in response to chronic stress.

questions.text: Which of the following is considered a character of epithelial tissue?
questions.explanation: Apical, lateral and basal epithelial surfaces have different structures/functions. Distinguishing alternatives: Epithelial cells are often specialized/modified; Epithelium is avascular; Many epithelia renew rather than being permanently differentiated; Cells are close together.

questions.text: All of the following are features of epithelial tissue EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: No blood vessels pass between epithelial cells; underlying connective-tissue vessels supply them by diffusion.
options: Formed of cells with minimal intercellular substance
Cells are penetrated by blood vessels

questions.text: Which type of the following structure completely prevents passage of substances between adjacent cells?
questions.explanation: Tight junctions seal the paracellular pathway between adjacent epithelial cells. Distinguishing alternatives: Hemidesmosomes anchor to matrix; Gap junctions communicate; Adherens junctions anchor; Interdigitations mechanically interlock surfaces.

questions.text: The dense plaque in the cytoplasmic aspects of the adjacent cells of the prickle cell layer in the epidermis of the skin is associated with...
questions.explanation: Epidermal desmosomes link keratin intermediate filaments to cytoplasmic dense plaques. Distinguishing alternatives: Actin attaches to adherens junctions; Claudin is tight-junction protein; Vimentin is mesenchymal intermediate filament; Laminin is basal-lamina matrix.

questions.text: Cardiac muscle fibres are acting together in a coordinated manner due to the presence of.,..
questions.explanation: Gap junctions permit electrical coupling of cardiac muscle cells. Distinguishing alternatives: Desmosomes anchor; Tight junctions seal; Zonula adherens anchors; Fascia adherens mechanically links myofibrils.

questions.text: Which of the following is a characteristic of the terminal web of the epithelial cells?
questions.explanation: The terminal web is an apical actin/intermediate-filament network beneath microvilli. Distinguishing alternatives: It is apical rather than basal; Axoneme belongs to cilium; Basal body belongs to cilium; Mitochondria characterize basal ion-transport folds.
options: It is located at the basal cytoplasm of the cell.
It is associated with the axoneme of the cilia.
It is associated with the basal body of the cilia,
It is formed of actin and intermediate filaments

questions.text: Desmosomes:
questions.explanation: Desmosomes mechanically couple cells through keratin intermediate filaments. Distinguishing alternatives: Nexus means gap junction; Molecule passage is gap-junction function; Connexons are gap-junction channels.
options: Permits passage of molecules from one cell to another
The transmembrane protein is called connexons
Is supported by Keratin = tono filaments

questions.text: Connexins are transmembrane protein present in:
questions.explanation: Connexin subunits make connexon channels in gap junctions. Distinguishing alternatives: Tight junction does not use connexons; Fascia occludens seals; Adherens junction anchors; Desmosomes anchor intermediate filaments.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a part of the junctional complex?
questions.explanation: The epithelial apical complex contains occludens, adherens and desmosomes, excluding gap junctions. Distinguishing alternatives: Zonula adherens is included; Macula adherens is included; Zonula occludens is included; Desmosomes are macula adherens and included.

questions.text: Epithelial cells have membrane channels that permit ions and small signalling molecules to pass between adjacent cells. Which of the following proteins forms these intercellular junctions?
questions.explanation: Gap-junction connexin channels pass ions and small signaling molecules directly between cells. Distinguishing alternatives: Claudins seal tight junctions; Cadherins anchor cells; Integrins bind matrix/hemidesmosomal attachments; Laminin is extracellular basal-lamina protein.

questions.text: The basal surfaces of cells lining distal convoluted (renal) tubules are characterized by presence of
questions.explanation: Distal renal tubular ion transport is supported by basal folds and nearby mitochondria. Distinguishing alternatives: Desmosomes are lateral anchoring junctions; Nexus is a communicating junction; Interdigitations are lateral; Microvilli are apical.

questions.text: A dense network of cytoskeletal filaments in the apical cytoplasm of the epithelial cells is called....
questions.explanation: The terminal web supports microvillar bases in the apical cytoplasm. Distinguishing alternatives: Basal body is ciliary base; Axoneme is ciliary shaft; MTOC organizes microtubules; Centrosome lies near nucleus.

questions.text: Each of the following statements concerning the epithelium is true EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Epithelial thickness varies with tissue type and can change markedly with urothelial distension. Distinguishing alternatives: Strong lateral adhesion is supported; Avascularity is supported; Polarity is supported.
options: They have a strong lateral adhesions.
They do not contain blood vesseles.

questions.text: Each of the following statements concerning st. squamus epith. is true EXCEPT;
questions.explanation: Only superficial cells reach the apical surface in true stratified epithelium. Distinguishing alternatives: Superficial squamous shape defines the type; Keratinized form occurs in skin; Basal cells have hemidesmosomal attachments.
options: All cells reach the apical surface.
It is found in the skin.

questions.text: Each of the following statement concerning stratified epithelium is true EXCEPT;
questions.explanation: Only basal-layer cells rest on basal lamina in true stratified epithelium. Distinguishing alternatives: Oesophagus has stratified squamous; Stratified squamous can keratinize; Epidermis is stratified squamous.
options: All of its cells rest on basement membrane.

questions.text: A 48-year-old man complains of painful ulcers in his mouth. Further examination reveals inflammation of the mucosa of his oesophagus. Which type of epithelia lines the oesophagus?
questions.explanation: Oesophageal mucosa is nonkeratinized stratified squamous epithelium. Distinguishing alternatives: Keratinized is epidermal; Columnar stratified is not normal oesophageal; Cuboidal is not normal oesophageal; Simple columnar is not normal oesophageal.

questions.text: Blood capillaries are lined by...
questions.explanation: Endothelium is the simple squamous lining of blood vessels. Distinguishing alternatives: Mesothelium lines serous cavities; Neurothelium is not the vascular lining; Transitional lines urinary passages.

questions.text: Stratified squamous non-keratinized epithelium can be found in:
questions.explanation: Oral cavity has wet protective nonkeratinized stratified squamous epithelium. Distinguishing alternatives: Palm is keratinized; Stomach is simple columnar; Bladder is transitional.

questions.text: Pseudostratified columnar epithelium is found in:
questions.explanation: Tracheal respiratory epithelium is pseudostratified ciliated columnar. Distinguishing alternatives: Skin has stratified squamous; Vessels have simple squamous; Most urinary passages have transitional lining.

questions.text: Endothelium is the lining epithelium of:
questions.explanation: Endothelium lines blood and lymphatic vessels. Distinguishing alternatives: Pleura mesothelium; Alveolar epithelium; Bowman not endothelial; Serous mesothelium.

questions.text: Which type of epithelium can withstand distention?
questions.explanation: Transitional epithelium adapts cell shape and apparent layer count to distension. Distinguishing alternatives: Keratinized squamous protects; Nonkeratinized squamous protects; Stratified columnar is not the named distensible type.

questions.text: By L/M examination, cells lining mucous acini have...
questions.explanation: Mucous acinar cells have basal flattened nuclei and pale vacuolated cytoplasm. Distinguishing alternatives: Apical acidophilic granules are serous; Deep acidophilia is not mucous pattern; Rounded nuclei characterize serous; Long contractile processes characterize myoepithelium.

questions.text: reversible abnormal change in the type of lining epithelium of a tissue is called
questions.explanation: Metaplasia is a reversible replacement of one differentiated cell type by another. Distinguishing alternatives: Dysplasia is disordered maturation/growth; Neoplasia is autonomous tumor growth; Elasticity is mechanical recoil; Plasticity is a broader adaptability term.

questions.text: The pleura of lung is lined by:
questions.explanation: Pleura is a serous membrane lined by mesothelium. Distinguishing alternatives: Endothelium lines vessels; Neurothelium is not pleural lining; Transitional is urinary; Myoepithelium is contractile gland support.

questions.text: The lining epithelium of the Fallopian (uterine tube) is.
questions.explanation: The uterine tube has simple columnar epithelium with ciliated and secretory cells. Distinguishing alternatives: Goblet cells are not normal tubal secretory cells; Pseudostratified goblet-cell lining is respiratory; Pseudostratified is not normal uterine tube; Stereociliated pseudostratified is epididymal.
options: Simple columnar ciliated with goblet cell
Pseudo stratified columnar with goblet cell

questions.text: In a merocrine secreting cell, the secretory materials go out by
questions.explanation: Merocrine secretion is exocytosis without loss of apical cytoplasm or the whole cell. Distinguishing alternatives: Cell disintegration is holocrine; Phagocytosis ingests particles; Apical shedding is apocrine; Pinocytosis ingests fluid.
options: Shedding of apical part of the cell

questions.text: Holocrine secretion:
questions.explanation: Sebaceous glands release the entire disintegrating cell. Distinguishing alternatives: Not endocrine type; Apical only apocrine; Intact merocrine; Not all.
options: Involve destruction of the apical parts of the cell.
Involve no change in secretory cells.

questions.text: Mucous secreting cells are characterized by:
questions.explanation: Mucous cells show pale basophilic vacuolated cytoplasm because routine preparation poorly stains their mucin.
options: Rich with mitochondria and smooth endoplasmic reticulum.
Have central round nucleus with prominent nucleolus.
Have vacuolated and pale basophilic cytoplasm.

questions.text: Taste buds are example of:
questions.explanation: Taste buds are neuroepithelium containing sensory, supporting and basal cells. Distinguishing alternatives: Myoepithelium contracts; Stratified describes surrounding lining rather than taste-bud specialization; Glandular secretes; Absorptive epithelium transports nutrients.

questions.text: Droplets of lipid are secreted in the mammary gland by which of following pathway?
questions.explanation: The milk lipid component buds with an apical cytoplasmic envelope by apocrine secretion. Distinguishing alternatives: Endocrine describes blood-borne signaling; Paracrine describes nearby signaling; Merocrine releases soluble proteins without cytoplasmic loss; Holocrine releases the whole cell.

questions.text: an example of apocrine secretion:
questions.explanation: Lipid secretion by lactating mammary glands uses apocrine release of apical cytoplasm.

questions.text: endothelium lining of blood vessels is an example of :
questions.explanation: Vascular endothelium is a single layer of flattened squamous cells.

questions.text: gall bladder lining is formed of:
questions.explanation: Gallbladder mucosa consists of nonciliated simple columnar absorptive epithelial cells.

questions.text: in hemidesmosome , the transmembrane adhesion molecule is:
questions.explanation: Hemidesmosomal integrins link basal epithelial plaques to the basal lamina.

questions.text: occluding junction with transmission E.M appear to have:
questions.explanation: Tight-junction membrane apposition produces a pentalaminar appearance with three dense and two lucent lines.
options: Its cytoplasmic surface attached to tonofilaments

questions.text: About Gap junction (Nexus), all true except:
questions.explanation: Gap channels join two six-connexin connexons and couple cells electrically/metabolically; epidermal anchoring is characterized by desmosomes.
options: Present between cardiac muscles & bone cells

questions.text: Terminal web is attached to:
questions.explanation: Actin of the apical terminal web connects with the circumferential zonula adherens.

questions.text: Epidermal cells of skin are richly anchored together by:
questions.explanation: Epidermal desmosomes anchor keratin intermediate filaments to strong cell-to-cell plaques.

questions.text: Basal cell membrane infoldings & elongated mitochondria are found in:
questions.explanation: Basal membrane folds increase transport area, while adjacent elongated mitochondria supply ATP for ion pumping.
options: Ion transporting cells e.g. convoluted tubules of kidney
Steroid forming cells e.g. adrenal cortex cells
Protein secreting cells e.g pancreatic acini

questions.text: The epithelium is characterized by:
questions.explanation: Epithelium lies on a basement membrane of variable LM visibility. Distinguishing alternatives: High renewal; Narrow spaces; Avascular; Nerves present.
options: It has low power of regeneration.
It consists of cells with wide intercellular spaces.
It is penetrated by blood vessels.
Clear or non clear basement membrane.

questions.text: The surface epithelium:
questions.explanation: Surface epithelium covers external surfaces and lines cavities. Distinguishing alternatives: Glandular subtype; Myoepithelium; Neuroepithelium; Little extracellular space.

questions.text: One of the following characteristics is true about epithelium:
questions.explanation: Basement membrane separates epithelium from CT. Distinguishing alternatives: Little matrix; Avascular; High renewal; Nerves can enter.
options: Contains large amounts of intercellular substance.
Separated from C.T by basement membrane.
Do not have a high power of regeneration.

questions.text: Simple squamous epithelium is formed of:
questions.explanation: Simple squamous means one layer of flattened cells with flattened nuclei. Distinguishing alternatives: Cubical wrong; Round nuclei not typical; Two layers not simple; Different heights pseudo.
options: One layer of cube-like cells with flat nuclei.
One layer of flat cells with rounded nuclei.
One layer of flat cells with flat nuclei.
Two layers of flat cells with flat nuclei.
One layer of flat cells with nuclei at more than one level.

questions.text: Simple squamous epithelium can be found in:
questions.explanation: Alveoli have thin type I squamous epithelium. Distinguishing alternatives: Intestine columnar; Trachea pseudo; Gallbladder columnar; Thyroid cuboidal.

questions.text: Mesothelium is the lining epithelium of:
questions.explanation: Pleura is lined by mesothelium. Distinguishing alternatives: Alveolar not; Blood endothelium; Thyroid cuboidal; Tube columnar.

questions.text: The following statement is true regarding simple squamous epithelium:
questions.explanation: Serous mesothelium is simple squamous. Distinguishing alternatives: Avascular; Single layer; Intestine columnar; Thyroid cuboidal.
options: It’s formed of many layers of cells.
It forms the mesothelium of serous membranes.

questions.text: One of the followings is not a site of simple squamous epithelium:
questions.explanation: Proximal convoluted tubules have simple cuboidal epithelium with microvilli. Distinguishing alternatives: Bowman parietal squamous; Alveoli squamous; Lymphatic endothelium; Vascular endothelium.

questions.text: Simple squamous epithelium is suitable for
questions.explanation: Thin alveolar squamous epithelium facilitates gas diffusion. Distinguishing alternatives: Not principal secretion; Reabsorption other cells; Thick stratified stronger protection; Myo contractile.

questions.text: One of the followings is NOT lined with simple squamous epithelium:
questions.explanation: Thyroid follicles normally have cuboidal rather than squamous epithelium. Distinguishing alternatives: Aortic endothelium; Pericardial mesothelium; Alveoli squamous; Bowman parietal squamous.

questions.text: In absorbing cubical cell, the brush border seen by L/M is:
questions.explanation: Brush border consists of densely packed microvilli. Distinguishing alternatives: Cilia motile; Flagellum sperm; Stereocilia long elsewhere; Desmosome junction.

questions.text: Simple cubical epithelium is found in:
questions.explanation: Thyroid follicles are the explicit cuboidal site. Distinguishing alternatives: Gallbladder columnar; Alveoli squamous; Bladder transitional; Trachea pseudo.

questions.text: The function of simple columnar epithelium is:
questions.explanation: Columnar epithelium is specialized for both secretion and absorption. Distinguishing alternatives: Only secretion too narrow; Only absorption too narrow; Squamous filtration; Protection less distinctive.

questions.text: Pseudo-stratified columnar ciliated epithelium can be found in:
questions.explanation: Trachea and large bronchi/upper respiratory passages have ciliated pseudostratified epithelium. Distinguishing alternatives: Ovary not; Vessel squamous; Urinary transitional; Bronchioles simple.

questions.text: One statement about pseudo-stratified columnar ciliated epithelium is true:
questions.explanation: All cells contact basement membrane although not all reach lumen. Distinguishing alternatives: Not keratinized; Avascular; Actually single layer; Includes short basal cells.
options: All cells resting on a basement membrane.
It is a type of stratified epithelium.
All cells are tall columnar cells.

questions.text: Simple columnar ciliated epithelium is found in:
questions.explanation: Fallopian tube has simple ciliated columnar cells. Distinguishing alternatives: Intestinal microvilli; Gastric secretory; Trachea pseudo; Nasal respiratory pseudo.

questions.text: The following statement is true regarding stratified squamous epithelium:
questions.explanation: Esophagus is nonkeratinized stratified squamous. Distinguishing alternatives: Not always keratinized; Superficial squamous; Mucoid claim not characteristic; Basement membrane present.
options: The superficial layer of cells always keratinized.
It lines the wall of the oesophagus.
Its most superficial layer of cells is cuboidal cells.
The intercellular spaces contain mucoid-like substance.

questions.text: The following statement is true concerning stratified squamous epithelium:
questions.explanation: Desmosomes link stratified squamous epithelial cells. Distinguishing alternatives: Not always keratinized; Trachea pseudo; Only basal layer on BM; Variable layers.
options: All its cells rest on the basement membrane.

questions.text: One statement about transitional epithelium is true:
questions.explanation: Superficial umbrella cells may be binucleated. Distinguishing alternatives: Urinary not respiratory; Not a transitional lineage between two types; No stereocilia; Visibility not defining.
options: Represent a transitional tissue between stratified squamous and stratified columnar epithelium.
Has stereocilia as a surface modification.
The upper most layers have binucleated cells.

questions.text: One of the following organs is lined with transitional epithelium:
questions.explanation: Urinary bladder is urothelial. Distinguishing alternatives: Uterus columnar; Vas pseudo; Gallbladder columnar; Intestine columnar.

questions.text: Urinary bladder is lined with:
questions.explanation: Bladder lining is transitional epithelium. Distinguishing alternatives: Pseudo wrong; Columnar wrong; Squamous wrong; Cubical wrong.

questions.text: One of the following organs is NOT lined with transitional epithelium:
questions.explanation: Uterus has columnar rather than transitional lining. Distinguishing alternatives: Pelvis transitional; Ureter transitional; Bladder transitional; Prostatic urethra transitional proximally.

questions.text: Transitional epithelium is found in:
questions.explanation: Urinary bladder is the listed transitional site. Distinguishing alternatives: Gallbladder columnar; Uterus columnar; PCT cuboidal; Trachea pseudo.

questions.text: One statement is true about stratified columnar epithelium:
questions.explanation: Stratified epithelia are named by surface-cell shape. Distinguishing alternatives: BM visibility not decisive; Surface not flat; Skin squamous; Basal not flat.
options: It rests on non/clear & non-wavy basement membrane.
The surface cells are columnar in shape.

questions.text: Exocrine glands:
questions.explanation: Exocrine glands deliver secretions through ducts onto epithelial surfaces. Distinguishing alternatives: Uni and multicellular; Blood endocrine; Hormones endocrine generally; Several secretion modes.
options: Discharge secretory product by diffusion into the blood.

questions.text: In heavy smokers, the pseudo-stratified columnar ciliated epithelium of the bronchi may transform to:
questions.explanation: Chronic smoking can replace bronchial respiratory epithelium with stratified squamous. Distinguishing alternatives: Simple wrong; Ciliated stratified wrong; Columnar stratified wrong; Cubical wrong.

questions.text: Parotid gland is considered:
questions.explanation: University atlas identifies parotid as a serous exocrine gland. Distinguishing alternatives: Not mucous; Not mixed normally; Multicellular; Not endocrine.

questions.text: Intestinal glands are considered as:
questions.explanation: Intestinal crypts are simple tubular glands, verified in university atlas. Distinguishing alternatives: Not branched crypt architecture; Not compound; Not coiled; Not alveolar.

questions.text: Glandular epithelium is classified according to mode of secretion into:
questions.explanation: Holocrine secretion releases destroyed secretory cells. Distinguishing alternatives: Apocrine loses apex; Merocrine intact; Cell number not mode; Salivary multicellular.
options: Apocrine where no change occurs in the secretory cells.
Merocrine where the apex of the cell is destroyed during secretion.
Multicellular gland as the sweat gland.
Holocrine where the cells are destroyed during secretion.

questions.text: Simple branched tubular glands:
questions.explanation: Simple means unbranched duct; branched modifies secretory units. Distinguishing alternatives: Duct unbranched; Exocrine; Tubular not alveolar; Secretory branches.

questions.text: Myoepithelial cells are:
questions.explanation: Basket cells surround salivary acini and contain actin plus myosin. Distinguishing alternatives: Thyroid no; Not myosin only; Pancreatic acini lack typical basket cells; Suprarenal no.
options: Present around acini of salivary glands.

questions.text: Stereocilia are:
questions.explanation: Stereocilia are long nonmotile microvilli. Distinguishing alternatives: Not short; Not motile axoneme; Not true cilia; Restricted sites.

questions.text: One of the following is a character of cilia:
questions.explanation: Ciliary axoneme contains microtubule doublets. Distinguishing alternatives: Microvilli absorb; Renal brush microvilli; Intestinal brush microvilli; Actin microvilli.
options: They increase surface area for absorption.
They form the brush border in cells lining the renal tubules.
They form the brush border in cells lining the intestine

questions.text: Gap junction is characterized by:
questions.explanation: Connexons permit ions and small molecules to pass between cells. Distinguishing alternatives: Desmosome stress; Adherens adhesive; Adherens actin; Gap2–3 nm.
options: Present at site of mechanical stress e.g. friction.
Intercellular space filled with adhesive material.
Condensation of actin at the cytoplasmic side of the plasma membrane.
The adjacent cells are separated by 30 nm space.

questions.text: Macula adherence (desmosome) is characterized by:
questions.explanation: Keratin tonofilaments attach to desmosomal plaques. Distinguishing alternatives: Spot not belt; Gap passage; Gap communication; 15–30 nm not tiny gap.
options: Bundles of tonofilaments are anchored to the plaques.
Very narrow gap between the cells.

questions.text: In zonula adherens, the distance between 2 cell membranes is:
questions.explanation: Book gives15–20 nm intercellular gap at adherens junction. Distinguishing alternatives: 0 wrong; 2 gapjunction; 20 micrometers wrong; 0.2 wrong.

questions.text: Concerning zonula adherens, one statement is true:
questions.explanation: Zonula adherens encircles cell as an actin-linked belt. Distinguishing alternatives: Tonofilaments desmosome; Channels gap; Disc macula; Strongest unsupported absolute.
options: Tonofilaments are inserted into the plaques forming hairpin-like structures.
The adjacent cells are separated by a narrow gap, crossed by communicating channels.
It is a disk shaped junction between epithelial cells.
It encircles the cell like a belt.

questions.text: Ion transporting cells are characterized by:
questions.explanation: Basal infoldings with mitochondria increase ion transport surface and energy supply. Distinguishing alternatives: Lateral not defining; Skeletal not listed epithelium; Cilia movement; Many mitochondria.

questions.text: In microvilli thick myosin filaments form their core to keep their shape.
questions.explanation: Microvillus cores consist of actin microfilaments, with associated myosin at membrane attachments.

questions.text: Salivary glands are merocrine while sebaceous glands are apocrine.
questions.explanation: Salivary glands are merocrine; sebaceous are holocrine.

questions.text: Myoepithelial cells are found around acini of sebaceous glands.
questions.explanation: Myoepithelial cells surround salivary/mammary secretory units rather than sebaceous holocrine acini.

questions.text: The secretion of parotid gland is serous.
questions.explanation: Opened university atlas identifies parotid serous secretion.

questions.text: Neuroepithelium is present in salivary glands.
questions.explanation: Salivary gland is secretory glandular epithelium; taste/olfactory epithelium are sensory.

questions.text: Pseudostratified columnar ciliated is present in trachea.
questions.explanation: Trachea has ciliated pseudostratified columnar epithelium.

questions.text: The epithelium lining the blood capillaries is called endothelium.
questions.explanation: Capillary lining is endothelium.

questions.text: The epithelium lining the serous membranes is called mesothelium.
questions.explanation: Serous membranes are lined by mesothelium.

questions.text: In transitional epithelium, the cells are joined by desmosomes.
questions.explanation: Urothelial cells have desmosomal adhesion as well as surface tight junctions.

questions.text: In transitional epithelium, the superficial cells may be binucleated.
questions.explanation: Umbrella cells may have two nuclei.

questions.text: Urinary bladder is lined with transitional epithelium.
questions.explanation: Urinary bladder lining is transitional urothelium.

questions.text: In gap junction, the cells are separated by wide intercellular space.
questions.explanation: Gap junction membranes are separated by a narrow2–3 nm space.

questions.text: Epithelium of the gastro-intestinal tract is mesodermal in origin.
questions.explanation: Digestive lining is predominantly endodermal with ectodermal terminal regions, not mesodermal.

questions.text: Pseudostratified columnar epithelium is suitable for gases exchange.
questions.explanation: Alveolar simple squamous rather than thick pseudostratified lining permits efficient gas diffusion.

questions.text: Cells lining the epididymis are provided with motile cilia.
questions.explanation: Epididymal stereocilia are nonmotile long microvilli.

questions.text: In holocrine glands the tips of secretory cells are detached and come out with secretion.
questions.explanation: Apical cytoplasm shedding is apocrine; holocrine destroys/releases entire cell.

questions.text: Blood vessels can penetrate epithelial tissue.
questions.explanation: Epithelial tissue proper is avascular and supplied by diffusion from adjacent CT.

questions.text: Absorptive cells are provided with microvilli to increase surface area for absorption.
questions.explanation: Microvilli increase absorptive surface area.

questions.text: Match Column (A) with Column (B).
questions.explanation: The aorta has simple squamous endothelium; the esophagus has nonkeratinized stratified squamous epithelium. Bladder urothelium is transitional, tracheal epithelium is pseudostratified columnar, and thyroid follicles are simple cuboidal.

questions.text: The epithelium lines the urinary bladder is :
questions.explanation: Transitional epithelium lines the urinary bladder and accommodates distension. Distinguishing alternatives: Simple squamous does not provide bladder urothelium; Stratified squamous is not the normal bladder lining; Glandular epithelium is not the bladder lining.

questions.text: The epithelium that lines the blood vessels is called :
questions.explanation: Endothelium is the simple squamous epithelial lining of blood vessels. Distinguishing alternatives: Mesothelium lines serous cavities; Transitional epithelium lines urinary passages; Pseudostratified epithelium lines examples such as trachea.

questions.text: The trachea (upper respiratory tract) is lined by :
questions.explanation: Respiratory epithelium in the trachea is pseudostratified ciliated columnar with goblet cells. Distinguishing alternatives: Simple squamous is alveolar/endothelial; Nonkeratinized stratified squamous lines wet protective surfaces; Keratinized stratified squamous forms epidermis.
options: pseudostratified columnar ciliated epithelium with goblet cells

questions.text: The epithelium which is formed of more than one layer is called :
questions.explanation: Stratified epithelium has two or more real cell layers. Distinguishing alternatives: Simple has one layer; Pseudostratified is a single layer with staggered nuclei; All cannot apply.

questions.text: The epidermis is formed by:
questions.explanation: Epidermis is keratinized stratified squamous epithelium. Distinguishing alternatives: Not the epidermal classification; Nonkeratinized type lines wet surfaces; Ciliated columnar is not epidermis.

questions.text: The epithelium type that line most of the gastrointestinal tract is:
questions.explanation: Most gastrointestinal mucosa is simple columnar, modified for secretion or absorption. Distinguishing alternatives: Squamous is limited to particular protective segments; Cuboidal is not the predominant GI mucosal type; Transitional belongs to urinary tract.

questions.text: The alveoli in the lung (gas exchange) are line by :
questions.explanation: Thin simple squamous alveolar lining enables gas exchange. Distinguishing alternatives: Cuboidal type-II cells exist but are not the principal gas-exchange surface; Columnar cells would impede diffusion; Pseudostratified is conducting airway epithelium.

questions.text: The epithelium that lines the abdominal cavity (peritoneum)\(serous sacs) is called :
questions.explanation: Mesothelium lines the peritoneal and other serous cavities. Distinguishing alternatives: Endothelium lines vessels; Transitional lines urinary tract; Epithelioid is not the serous-lining name.

questions.text: The epithelium which is composed of cells resting on the same basement membrane , but not all reaching the lumen is called:
questions.explanation: Pseudostratified cells all contact the basal lamina but some do not reach the free surface. Distinguishing alternatives: True stratified squamous has several layers; Stratified cuboidal has multiple real layers; Transitional has multiple distensible layers.

questions.text: The oesophagous is lined by:
questions.explanation: Human esophagus is lined by nonkeratinized stratified squamous epithelium.

questions.text: The epithelium forming the taste buds is:
questions.explanation: Taste buds contain sensory, supporting and basal cells forming neuroepithelium. Distinguishing alternatives: Glandular cells secrete; Simple is not the specific sensory category; Stratified refers to surrounding lining rather than the taste-bud specialization.

questions.text: Function of stratified epithelium is:
questions.explanation: Stratification principally provides protection against mechanical injury.

questions.text: The surface of simple squamous epithelium is thin to allow:
questions.explanation: The thin squamous layer minimizes diffusion distance for material exchange. Distinguishing alternatives: Ease of movement chiefly follows from smoothness; The combined option does not distinguish the specified structural property.

questions.text: The surface of simple squamous epithelium is smooth to allow:
questions.explanation: The smooth squamous lining reduces friction for blood flow and visceral movement. Distinguishing alternatives: Exchange principally depends on a thin diffusion barrier; Combining unrelated thinness and smoothness effects loses the requested distinction.
options: passage of blood & easy movement of organs

questions.text: The lining epithelium of thyroid follicles is:
questions.explanation: Normal thyroid follicles are usually lined by simple cuboidal follicular cells.

questions.text: The lining epithelium of the uterus is:
questions.explanation: The uterine lining is simple columnar with ciliated and secretory cells. Distinguishing alternatives: Squamous is not normal endometrial; Cuboidal is not the general uterine surface lining; Transitional is urinary.

questions.text: The lining epithelium of the ureter is:
questions.explanation: Ureters are lined by distensible transitional epithelium. Distinguishing alternatives: Simple squamous is not ureteral; Cuboidal is not the ureteral lining; Ciliated columnar is not ureteral.

questions.text: The origin of the epithelium is :
questions.explanation: Epithelial tissue can arise from any of the three embryonic germ layers. Distinguishing alternatives: Ectodermal origin exists; Mesodermal origin exists; Endodermal origin exists.

questions.text: The epithelium is charactercized by :
questions.explanation: Epithelial cells are avascular and obtain nutrients from underlying connective-tissue vessels. Distinguishing alternatives: Blood vessels do not enter between epithelial cells; Intercellular material is minimal; Epithelial cells rest on basal lamina.

questions.text: which of the following has supporting cells:
questions.explanation: Neuroepithelium has sensory cells supported by supporting and basal cells. Distinguishing alternatives: Simple is a layer classification; Stratified is a layer classification; Glandular epithelium is primarily secretory.

questions.text: Nuclei of simple columnar epithelium are:
questions.explanation: Simple columnar cells have basal oval nuclei. Distinguishing alternatives: Central rounded describes cuboidal; Flat describes squamous; Binucleation is not the general columnar pattern.

questions.text: Nuclei of simple cuboidal epithelium are:
questions.explanation: Simple cuboidal cells have single rounded central nuclei. Distinguishing alternatives: Basal oval describes columnar; Flat describes squamous; Binucleation is not the general cuboidal pattern.

questions.text: The type of epithelium that can accommodate stretch is:
questions.explanation: Transitional epithelium changes surface-cell shape and apparent layer count during distension. Distinguishing alternatives: Squamous stratified protects but is not specialized urothelium; Stratified columnar is not the named distensible type; Pseudostratified is not the named distensible type.

questions.text: ion transporting cells need large surface area , so they are characterized by:
questions.explanation: Basal infoldings associated with mitochondria enlarge the surface for ion transport. Distinguishing alternatives: Microvilli chiefly enlarge apical absorptive surface; Interdigitations link lateral borders; Canaliculi are not this epithelial specialization.

questions.text: Epithelium is characterized by :
questions.explanation: Epithelial cells rest on basal lamina and have little extracellular material. Distinguishing alternatives: Epithelium is avascular; Matrix is minimal; Epithelium can receive sensory nerves.

questions.text: cell junction that prevent leakage (passage of fluids) is :
questions.explanation: Zonula occludens seals the paracellular space against leakage. Distinguishing alternatives: Gap junctions provide communication; Zonula adherens anchors cells without making the seal.

questions.text: serous acini are characterized by the following except :
questions.explanation: Serous acini have narrow lumina, rounded nuclei and apical protein granules; pale vacuolation characterizes mucous acini.

questions.text: mucous acini are characterized by all of the following except:
questions.explanation: Mucous acini secrete viscous mucin, while enzyme-rich watery secretion is serous. Distinguishing alternatives: Basal flattened nucleus is mucous; Wide lumen is mucous; Cuboidal secretory cells are mucous in the course.

questions.text: The type of filaments present in zonula adherens (adhering jun.) is :
questions.explanation: Zonula adherens links the actin cytoskeleton to the junctional plaque. Distinguishing alternatives: Intermediate keratin filaments attach to desmosomes; Myosin is not the specified plaque attachment.

questions.text: intercellular space is zero in :
questions.explanation: Tight junctions bring membranes together to close the paracellular space in the course ultrastructural description.

questions.text: sterocilia is characterized by:
questions.explanation: Stereocilia are long immotile microvilli with actin cores. Distinguishing alternatives: They are not short motile structures; They are not motile cilia; Microtubules form cilia rather than stereocilia cores.

questions.text: connexin protein is found in :
questions.explanation: Connexin subunits assemble into connexon channels of gap junctions. Distinguishing alternatives: Desmosomes use adhesion-linker proteins; Adherens junctions anchor cytoskeleton via adhesion proteins; Tight junctions seal via other transmembrane proteins.

questions.text: communicating junction :
questions.explanation: Gap junctions are the communicating junctions permitting intercellular passage of ions and small molecules.

questions.text: Basal infoldings in epithelial cells are present in :
questions.explanation: Ion-transporting epithelial cells have basal membrane folds with associated mitochondria. Distinguishing alternatives: Protein secretion emphasizes rER/Golgi; Steroid secretion emphasizes sER; Phagocytosis emphasizes lysosomes/vacuoles.

questions.text: glands that lose their upper portion of cytoplasm during secretion:
questions.explanation: Apocrine secretion releases an apical cytoplasmic portion together with the product. Distinguishing alternatives: Merocrine releases by exocytosis without loss; Holocrine loses the entire cell; Autocrine describes signaling back to the producing cell.

questions.text: glands that release their secretion by exocytosis is :
questions.explanation: Merocrine secretion is exocytosis without loss of cell substance. Distinguishing alternatives: Apocrine loses an apical portion; Holocrine loses the entire cell.

questions.text: salivary glands release their secretion by :
questions.explanation: Salivary cells release secretory products by merocrine exocytosis. Distinguishing alternatives: Apocrine loses cytoplasm; Holocrine loses the cell.

questions.text: sebaceous glands release their secretion by :
questions.explanation: Sebaceous cells accumulate lipid and disintegrate into the gland product. Distinguishing alternatives: Merocrine leaves the cell intact; Apocrine loses a portion.

questions.text: microvilli :
questions.explanation: Microvilli have actin cores and occur on absorptive intestinal and proximal renal tubular cells. Distinguishing alternatives: Microtubules characterize cilia; Actin core is true; Intestinal and proximal renal sites are true.

questions.text: the basal lamina is formed of :
questions.explanation: Basal lamina contains type-IV collagen and laminin. Distinguishing alternatives: Type III belongs to reticular lamina; Type VII forms anchoring fibrils; III and VII is the reticular-lamina combination.

questions.text: the reticular lamina is formed of :
questions.explanation: Reticular lamina contains type-III collagen and type-VII anchoring fibrils. Distinguishing alternatives: Type IV is basal lamina; Type III is present but incomplete; Type VII anchoring fibrils are present but incomplete.

questions.text: The basement membrane can be stained by:
questions.explanation: Basement membrane is PAS-positive and can be demonstrated by silver impregnation.
options: Both b and c are correct.

questions.text: junctional complex are:
questions.explanation: The intestinal junctional complex consists of zonula occludens, zonula adherens and desmosomes near the apical surface.
options: present in between small intestine epithelial cells

questions.text: myoepithelial cells are characterized by the following except:
questions.explanation: Myoepithelial cells are contractile cells between acinar cells and basal lamina and are more numerous in mucous/mixed acini.
options: present between base of cells & basement membrane

questions.text: Basal lamina by EM is formed of two layers:
questions.explanation: Conventional EM divides basal lamina into lamina lucida and lamina densa.

questions.text: Gap junction (nexus) is:
questions.explanation: Cardiac gap junctions permit ion exchange and electrical communication.

questions.text: Concerning the classification of the exocrine glands the term “simple” refers that:
questions.explanation: Simple refers to an unbranched duct, regardless of branching of its secretory units.
options: Its secretory part is one unit.

questions.text: Concerning the exocrine glands the term “tubular” refers to:
questions.explanation: Tubular refers to secretory-unit shape.
options: Its secretory part is one unit.

questions.text: Glands are classified according to the presence or absence of ducts into:
questions.explanation: Ducted glands are exocrine, ductless glands endocrine, and mixed glands contain both components.

questions.text: Pseudostratified columnar epithelium is a type of
questions.explanation: Pseudostratified epithelium is structurally one layer because every cell contacts basal lamina. Distinguishing alternatives: Stratified has several real layers; Glandular is a functional class, not the stated surface type; Neuroepithelium is sensory.

questions.text: All are true about goblet cell Except:
questions.explanation: A goblet cell is a single flask-shaped mucous gland scattered in intestinal or respiratory lining. Distinguishing alternatives: Mucus secretion is true; Flask shape is true; Respiratory site is true.

questions.text: Which of the following structure is lined by transitional epithelium:
questions.explanation: Ureteral urothelium is transitional and accommodates distension. Distinguishing alternatives: Epidermis is keratinized stratified squamous; Large intestine is simple columnar; Alveoli chiefly form a simple squamous gas-exchange surface.

questions.text: Which type of the epithelium has facet cells?
questions.explanation: Facet or umbrella cells are the superficial cells of transitional epithelium. Distinguishing alternatives: Cuboidal stratified lacks this specialization; Columnar stratified lacks facet cells; Squamous stratified has flattened superficial cells; Pseudostratified is a single layer.

questions.text: Cells of serous acinus have:
questions.explanation: Serous cells have apical acidophilic secretory granules and round nuclei around a narrow lumen.

questions.text: Which type of the epithelium has supporting cells ?
questions.explanation: Supporting cells are a named component of neuroepithelium. Distinguishing alternatives: Myoepithelium is contractile; Urothelium is transitional; Glandular epithelium is secretory.

questions.text: Cilia are found in the linning of the following except:
questions.explanation: Trachea, bronchi and uterine tube are ciliated; ordinary exocrine ducts are not the ciliated examples listed.

questions.text: Simple columnar epithelial lining of intestine is provided with:
questions.explanation: Intestinal microvilli contain actin and expand absorptive surface, unlike motile microtubule-based cilia.

questions.text: The base of microvilli is attached to:
questions.explanation: Actin bundles at microvillar bases extend into the apical terminal web. Distinguishing alternatives: Basal body anchors a cilium; Membrane covers the projection but is not its basal anchoring web; Basement membrane is at the opposite cell surface.

questions.text: This type of junctions seals the intercellular space:
questions.explanation: Occluding junctions seal the paracellular pathway, whereas anchoring and gap junctions have mechanical or communicating roles.

questions.text: Gap junction is present in the following cells except:
questions.explanation: Cardiac, smooth-muscle, some nerve and bone cells communicate through gap junctions; circulating blood cells do not form these stable networks.

questions.text: Salivary glands is an example of:
questions.explanation: Major salivary glands are compound exocrine glands with branched ducts delivering secretion to the oral cavity.

questions.text: Which of the followings is NOT a character of the epithelium:
questions.explanation: Epithelium has closely packed adherent cells and little matrix, and lacks blood and lymphatic vessels.

questions.text: What of the following facts about the epithelial tissue is true?
questions.explanation: Epithelial cells are supported by a basement membrane.
options: Epithelium is considered to be (vascular tissue).
It’s one of the C.T. fibers types.
Its cells lie on a basement membrane.
It’s transitional type is considered to be simple.

questions.text: The epithelium is characterized by:
questions.explanation: Epithelium is avascular and receives nutrients by diffusion from underlying connective tissue.

questions.text: The lining epithelium of pleura is:
questions.explanation: Pleural mesothelium is simple squamous epithelium.

questions.text: One statement is true:
questions.explanation: Simple squamous cells have flattened nuclei.
options: Simple squamous epithelium has flat nuclei.
Simple columnar epithelium present in the nasal surface of the soft palate.
Simple cuboidal epithelium forms the skin.
Simple squamous epithelium of two types; keratinized or non-keratinized.

questions.text: One statement is NOT true:
questions.explanation: Pseudostratified epithelial cells contain nuclei at different heights.
options: Pseudostratified columnar epithelium cells have no nuclei.

questions.text: The simple columnar non-ciliated epithelium is present in:
questions.explanation: Small intestine is lined by nonciliated simple columnar epithelium with an absorptive brush border.

questions.text: The simple cuboidal epithelium is present in:
questions.explanation: Thyroid follicles are usually lined by simple cuboidal follicular cells.

questions.text: Pseudostartified columnar ciliated epithelium is characterized by:
questions.explanation: Pseudostratified cells all contact basement membrane while nuclei occupy different heights.
options: Presence of several layers of cells.
The nuclei of cells are lying at the same height.
All cells are lying on the basement membrane.

questions.text: Goblet cells are present in:
questions.explanation: Respiratory ciliated pseudostratified epithelium contains goblet cells.

questions.text: Stratified epithelium formed of:
questions.explanation: Stratified epithelium has more than one cell layer.

questions.text: In the stratified squamous epithelium:
questions.explanation: The designated basal layer is columnar, with intermediate polyhedral and superficial squamous cells.
options: The basal layer is squamous cells.
The basal layer is columnar cells.
The basal layer is polyhydral cells.

questions.text: Stratified squamous keratinized epithelium:
questions.explanation: Keratinized stratified squamous epithelium has a superficial keratin layer.
options: Covered by thick layer of keratin.
Present in the moist surfaces (mouth, pharynx and esophagous).

questions.text: All the statements concerning the transitional epithelium is true EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Urothelial basal cells are not squamous; superficial cells change shape and may be binucleated.
options: The number of cell layers is changeable.

questions.text: All of the followings are examples of stratified epithelium EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Pseudostratified epithelium is one layer because every cell contacts basement membrane.

questions.text: The epithelium type that has the ability to decrease it’s layers number in full viscus is:
questions.explanation: Distended urothelium appears thinner as cells flatten and rearrange.

questions.text: The stratified squamous non-keratinized epithelium is present in:
questions.explanation: Vaginal epithelium is nonkeratinized stratified squamous.

questions.text: The stratified squamous keratinized epithelium is present in:
questions.explanation: Epidermis is keratinized stratified squamous.

questions.text: The epithelium that resist friction is:
questions.explanation: Stratified squamous epithelium resists abrasion.

questions.text: Facet cells of transitional epithelium:
questions.explanation: Superficial facet cells are large umbrella-like cells.

questions.text: According to the mode of secretion the exocrine glands classified into:
questions.explanation: Merocrine, apocrine and holocrine classify glands by release mechanism.

questions.text: Concerning the exocrine glands the term “compound” refers to:
questions.explanation: Compound denotes a branched duct system.

questions.text: Mixed gland is a mixture of:
questions.explanation: A mixed gland has endocrine and exocrine components, as in pancreas.

questions.text: Goblet cell:
questions.explanation: Goblet cells synthesize mucin and have basal compressed nuclei with developed secretory organelles.

questions.text: One of the following is a character of serous acini:
questions.explanation: Apical acidophilic zymogen granules characterize serous secretory cells.
options: They are larger in size than mucous acini.
The lining cells are highly vacuolated.
The lining cells have apical acidophilic granules.

questions.text: In mucus acini:
questions.explanation: Myoepithelial cells are numerous around mucous units.
options: The lining cells are flattened and contain flattened nuclei.

questions.text: Exocrine glands:
questions.explanation: Exocrine glands may be unicellular, such as goblet cells, or multicellular.
options: Have no connection with their site of origin.

questions.text: Concerning the myoepithelial cells all the statements are true EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Myoepithelial cells contain contractile filaments and surround exocrine secretory units rather than endocrine glands.
options: They are related to the endocrine glands.

questions.text: Which of the following epithelial cells has the ability to contract?
questions.explanation: Basket cells are contractile myoepithelial cells.

questions.text: One statement is true:
questions.explanation: Neuroepithelium is an epithelial specialization for sensory reception.
options: Neuroepithelium is a special type of nerve cells modified to epithelium.
Neuroepithelium is a special type of epithelium modified to sensory function.
Neuroepithelium means that nerve and epithelium are of the same origin.
Neuroepithelium means that epithelium develop from the nerve.

questions.text: The followings are free surface specialization EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Phagocytosis is an uptake process rather than a persistent free-surface specialization.

questions.text: Terminal web is:
questions.explanation: Terminal web is a subapical network including actin and intermediate filaments anchoring microvillus cores.
options: Complex of transversely actin and intermediate filaments.

questions.text: The actin filaments forms the core of the microvilli, it is embeded in:
questions.explanation: Microvillus actin roots insert into the terminal web.

questions.text: Microvilli under light microscope are described as:
questions.explanation: Dense microvilli form brush borders or striated borders depending on tissue terminology.

questions.text: One statement is true:
questions.explanation: Stereocilia are long actin-based microvilli, despite their name.
options: Stereocilia consists of 9 triplets of microtubules.

questions.text: Stereocilia have the following function/s:
questions.explanation: Stereocilia increase surface area in reproductive ducts and participate in sensory transduction in the ear.

questions.text: Zonula adherence:
questions.explanation: Zonula adherens is a belt-like actin-linked junction with a 15–20 nm intercellular gap, below the tight junction.
options: They are belt like junction with a space of 15-20 nm.
Prevents water soluble substances from passing between the cells.

questions.text: Desmosome (macula adherence):
questions.explanation: Desmosomes have dense attachment plaques, intermediate-filament insertion and a central dense line.
options: Disk shaped plaque of electron dense materials.

questions.text: Junctional complex is formed of three types of junctions:
questions.explanation: The apical junctional complex comprises tight junction, zonula adherens and desmosome.
options: Zonula occludene, zonula adherence and macula adherence.
Zonula occludene, zonula adherence and gap junction.

questions.text: Gap junction (nexus) is:
questions.explanation: Gap junctions are communicating channels between cells.

questions.text: All the following statements concerning gap junction (nexus) are true EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Gap junctions retain a narrow cleft crossed by paired connexons and do not fuse the membranes.
options: Minute structure bridging the gap called connexons.
Each connexon consists of six subunits.
Provides an actual fusion of adjacent two cell membranes.

questions.text: The following statements concerning gap junction (nexus) are true EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Gap-junction membranes remain separated by a narrow cleft bridged by connexons; they do not fuse.
options: It links the interior of adjacent cells.
It permits ions and small molecule to pass from one cell to other.
They transmit impulses at certain synapse.
Provides an actual fusion of adjacent two cell membranes.

questions.text: Concerning the basement membrane ONE statement is true:
questions.explanation: Basement membrane supports epithelium, with epithelial basal lamina and connective-tissue reticular lamina.
options: It is supporting layer between the epithelium and connective tissue.
Basal lamina synthesized by epithelial cells.
Lamina reticularis manufactured by connective tissue cells.

questions.text: The type of filaments present in macula adherens (desmosome) is:
questions.explanation: Desmosomes attach intermediate tonofilaments to their dense plaques; adherens belts instead attach actin.

questions.text: Which of the following is involved in cell to cell communication?
questions.explanation: Gap junctions directly connect neighboring cytoplasm through channels.

questions.text: The junction which prevents entrance of extracellular substance:
questions.explanation: Occluding junctions restrict paracellular passage of extracellular substances.

questions.text: Epithelial lining of serous sacs is called:
questions.explanation: Mesothelium is the simple squamous lining of serous sacs, distinct from vascular endothelium.

questions.text: Lining of blood vessels is called:
questions.explanation: Endothelium is the simple squamous lining of blood vessels, whereas mesothelium lines serous surfaces.

questions.text: Thyroid follicles are lined by:
questions.explanation: Normal follicular cells are typically cuboidal, becoming taller when active and flatter when inactive.

questions.text: Urinary bladder & ureter are lined by:
questions.explanation: Urinary bladder and ureter have transitional epithelium with distensible umbrella cells.

questions.text: Sebaceous gland is considered:
questions.explanation: Sebum is released by whole-cell breakdown, defining holocrine secretion.

questions.text: Tonofilaments (intermediate filaments) are attached to the following:
questions.explanation: Hemidesmosomes anchor basal epithelial intermediate filaments to basement membrane.

questions.text: The following junction appears pentalaminar in E.M.:
questions.explanation: Conventional EM shows a pentalaminar contact where neighboring membranes closely appose at tight junctions.

questions.text: The following junction has 7 electron dense lines with E.M.:
questions.explanation: Desmosome dense elements comprise two paired membrane profiles, two cytoplasmic plaques and a central line, giving the conventional seven-line description.

questions.text: The following junctions are attached to actin filaments except:
questions.explanation: Macula adherens attaches intermediate filaments; adherens junctions and tight-junction cytoplasmic complexes associate with actin.

questions.text: Conexons form the following junction:
questions.explanation: Paired connexons form communicating channels of gap junctions.

questions.text: Mucous acini are characterized by the following except:
questions.explanation: Mucous cells have pale mucin-rich cytoplasm and flat basal nuclei rather than serous apical zymogen granules.

questions.text: Urothelium: [lining of urinary bladder]
questions.explanation: Urothelium is the specialized transitional urinary lining that accommodates distension.

questions.text: Junction that forms a tight sealing of intercellular space:
questions.explanation: Tight junctions seal the extracellular paracellular route.

questions.text: Hemidesmosomes are attached to:
questions.explanation: Hemidesmosomes connect epithelial intermediate filaments to basement membrane through integrin-based adhesion.

subjects.name: Histology
subjects.lectures: Connective tissue organization and cell populations, Mesenchymal cells, pericytes and fibroblasts, Macrophages and the phagocyte system, Mast cells and allergic reactions, Plasma cells and antibodies, Adipose tissue, Collagen fibers and synthesis, Reticular fibers and stroma, Elastic fibers, Ground substance and extracellular matrix, Basement membrane, Loose and dense connective tissue, Embryonic connective tissue
lectureNames: Connective tissue organization and cell populations

questions.text: The origin of connective tissue is
questions.explanation: Designated course classifies connective tissue as mesodermal.

questions.text: Connective tissue differs from epithelial tissue in ....
questions.explanation: Connective tissue contains vessels within its abundant matrix; epithelial cell layers are avascular.
options: It is formed mainly of cells .
Its cells lie on basement membrane .
It is penetrated by blood vessels .

questions.text: Example of non sulphated glycosaminoclycans is:
questions.explanation: Hyaluronic acid is the nonsulfated glycosaminoglycan; heparin and dermatan are sulfated. Distinguishing alternatives: Heparin is sulfated; Histaman is not an established GAG option; Dermatan sulfate is sulfated.

questions.text: During collagen formation alpha chains form the triple helix procollagen in:
questions.explanation: Three pro-alpha chains assemble into a triple helix inside rER before Golgi transport. Distinguishing alternatives: Golgi packages later; Lysosomes digest; Secretory vesicles carry assembled product.

questions.text: During collagen formation fibroblasts exocytose:
questions.explanation: Fibroblasts exocytose procollagen, which is cleaved extracellularly. Distinguishing alternatives: Tropocollagen forms after cleavage; Single chains are assembled intracellularly; Dipeptides are not the collagen product.

questions.text: procollagen is converted into tropocollagen (collagen) molecules
questions.explanation: Extracellular procollagen peptidases remove terminal propeptides to generate collagen molecules. Distinguishing alternatives: Golgi packages procollagen; rER assembles procollagen; Lysosomes degrade material.

questions.text: Elastic fibers are formed by the following except:
questions.explanation: Elastic fibers are produced by fibroblasts, arterial smooth-muscle cells and chondroblasts; osteoblasts primarily produce bone matrix.
options: Smooth muscle cells in arterial blood vessels.

questions.text: Special stain for elastic fibers:
questions.explanation: Orcein and Van Gieson are the course's elastic-fiber staining methods. Distinguishing alternatives: Silver demonstrates reticular fibers; PAS demonstrates carbohydrates; Mallory is the collagen stain example.

questions.text: characteristic EM feature of collagen fibers:
questions.explanation: Regular staggered packing of collagen molecules produces axial periodicity. Distinguishing alternatives: Trilaminar describes membranes; Elastin core/microfibrils describes elastic fiber; Dense core/pale area is nonspecific.
options: central amorphous protein surrounded by microfibrils
electron dense core surrounded by pale area

questions.text: The structural units of collagen fibers are:
questions.explanation: Extracellular collagen molecules, tropocollagen, assemble into fibrils and fibers after propeptide removal.

questions.text: Short and thin anastomosing fibers in stroma of lymph node can be stained by...
questions.explanation: Fine branching lymph-node stroma consists of silver-positive reticular fibers. Distinguishing alternatives: H&E does not specifically demonstrate these fibers; Mallory demonstrates ordinary collagen; Sudan stains fat.

questions.text: Within the extracellular matrix of connective tissue, which of the following fibers are short, unbundled and positively stained with PAS stain & silver
questions.explanation: Reticular fibers are fine type-III collagen fibers with PAS-positive glycoprotein and silver affinity.

questions.text: Pericytes differ from macrophages by the presence of ....
questions.explanation: Pericytes have contractile actin and myosin, unlike the macrophage's dominant phagocytic specialization.

questions.text: Actin and myosin are numerous in the cytoplasm of which of the following cells?
questions.explanation: Pericytes regulate capillary flow through their contractile actin/myosin apparatus. Distinguishing alternatives: Plasma cells synthesize antibodies; Mast cells release mediators; Ordinary fibroblasts synthesize matrix, unlike contractile myofibroblasts; Pigment cells store pigment.

questions.text: In adult life , mesenchymal cells are present as:
questions.explanation: The course identifies pericytes as adult mesenchymal-derived cells associated with capillaries. Distinguishing alternatives: Large arteries use smooth-muscle media rather than capillary pericytes; Fibroblasts are differentiated matrix cells; Macrophages are monocyte-derived.

questions.text: Macrophages are specially stained with:
questions.explanation: Macrophages ingest injected trypan-blue dye during vital staining. Distinguishing alternatives: PAS detects carbohydrates; Toluidine metachromasia characterizes mast granules; Silver detects selected fibers/Golgi structures.

questions.text: All the following statements about mast cells are true Except:
questions.explanation: Mast cells contain dense mediator granules and high-affinity IgE receptors, not the characteristic IgA sensitizing specificity.
options: Can be stained metachromatically with toluidine blue
Provided with surface receptors for IgA immunoglobulins

questions.text: About plasma cell all are true except:
questions.explanation: Mature plasma cells are terminal antibody-secreting B-cell derivatives rather than the proliferating plasmablast stage.
options: Characterized by cart wheel shaped nucleus.

questions.text: Plasma cells and fibroblasts are similar in....
questions.explanation: Fibroblasts and plasma cells both synthesize large amounts of protein using rER and Golgi. Distinguishing alternatives: sER abundance describes lipid synthesis; Plasma cells are not branched fibroblasts; Clock-face nucleus characterizes plasma cells; Plasma cells make antibodies rather than collagen.
options: Having extensive RER and well developed Golgi
Having cart wheel appearance of the nucleus

questions.text: Fat droplets within adipocytes can be demonstrated with:
questions.explanation: Sudan III demonstrates lipid retained in appropriate preparations. Distinguishing alternatives: PAS stains carbohydrate; Silver is not fat-specific; Routine H&E dissolves much lipid and leaves empty spaces.

questions.text: The following are forms of embryonic connective tissue except:
questions.explanation: Mesenchymal and mucoid tissue are embryonic types; dense regular collagenous tissue is differentiated adult connective tissue.

questions.text: Protects newborn infants by heat production:
questions.explanation: Brown adipose tissue generates heat to protect newborns from cold. Distinguishing alternatives: White fat mainly stores/insulates; Mucoid tissue cushions; Reticular tissue supports cells.

questions.text: Dense regular white fibrous c.t. forms the following except:
questions.explanation: The liver capsule contains dense irregular connective tissue rather than parallel regular collagen bundles.

questions.text: About proteoglycans one is wrong:
questions.explanation: Laminin is a glycoprotein of basal lamina, whereas proteoglycans have protein cores with abundant GAG chains.
options: Formed of Glycosaminoglycans attached to core of protein.
Its carbohydrate portion is more than its protein.
Laminin is one of its examples.

questions.text: About glycoproteins all are true except:
questions.explanation: Adhesive glycoproteins bind cells and matrix; toluidine-blue metachromasia characterizes densely charged GAG-rich material rather than this glycoprotein class.
options: Formed mainly of protein to which carbohydrates are attached.
Act mainly as binding proteins between connective tissue components.
Important for adhesion between cells & intercellular substance.

questions.text: The following are found in basal lamina except:
questions.explanation: Basal lamina contains type-IV collagen, laminin and integrin-associated attachments; type II belongs to cartilage.

questions.text: About basement membrane all are true except:
questions.explanation: Lamina lucida and densa are zones of basal lamina, not reticular lamina. Distinguishing alternatives: III/VII reticular-lamina collagen is supported; IV collagen/laminin basal lamina is supported; LM/PAS basement-membrane visibility is supported.
options: Its lamina reticularis contains collagen type III & VII.
Its basal lamina contains collagen type IV & glycoproteins e.g. Laminin.
Can be seen by L.M. and stained with PAS.
Its lamina reticularis is divided into lamina densa & lucida.

questions.text: Reticular lamina of the basement membrane is formed by:
questions.explanation: Connective-tissue fibroblasts produce reticular lamina beneath basal lamina. Distinguishing alternatives: Epithelial cells produce basal lamina; Nerve-associated cells can have external lamina; Muscle cells have external lamina; Fat cells have external lamina.

questions.text: Regarding the dense regular C.T, one of the following statements is true:
questions.explanation: Parallel densely packed collagen bundles resist tensile load in one principal direction.
options: Is present in capsule of organs

questions.text: Regarding the collagen types, all true EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Fibroblasts synthesize collagen; typeIII supports reticular lamina and typeIV forms basal lamina. Elastoblast is not the designated collagen-producing cell class.
options: Collagen type III is present in reticular lamina
Collagen type IV present in basal lamina

questions.text: All true regarding reticular fibers EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Reticular fibers are glycoprotein-associated typeIII collagen, demonstrated by silver and PAS rather than reliably by routine H&E.

questions.text: All are stem cells (SC) EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: A mature red blood corpuscle lacks a nucleus and is terminally differentiated, not a stem cell.

questions.text: This type of collagen fibers are silver stained (argyrophilic) :
questions.explanation: Silver argyrophilia characterizes reticular fibers made of typeIII collagen.

questions.text: Tendon is a good example of this type of connective tissue:
questions.explanation: Tendon has parallel typeI collagen bundles and few fibrocytes, the dense regular pattern.
