questions.explanation: In this scurvy vignette, vitamin C deficiency impairs hydroxylation in rER during collagen synthesis; calcium, RBC and platelet deficits do not explain the collagen wound-healing pattern.

questions.text:
[A child comes to the pediatric outpatient clinic complaining of bleeding gums, falling of teeth and persistent non healing wounds. The attending resident suspected a disease related to connective tissue]. Answer the following:

This disease is due to:
questions.explanation: Vitamin C deficiency reduces collagen hydroxylation and maturation, causing fragile connective tissues, gingival bleeding and poor healing.
options: Rupture of RBCs due to their abnormal shapes.
Increased bone resorption over bone formation.

questions.text:
[A skin biopsy from an individual suffering from severe itching would demonstrate the presence of numerous number of certain connective tissue cell]. Answer the following:

This cell would be:
questions.explanation: Mast cells store/release histamine and mediate immediate hypersensitivity, making them the relevant CT cell for this severe-itching vignette; fibroblasts/reticular/pericytes provide support and plasma cells make antibodies.

questions.text:
[A skin biopsy from an individual suffering from severe itching would demonstrate the presence of numerous number of certain connective tissue cell]. Answer the following:

This cell produces:
questions.explanation: The identified mast cell releases histamine; antibodies belong to plasma cells, matrix fibers to fibroblastic cells and stored fat to adipocytes.

questions.text:
[A skin biopsy from an individual suffering from severe itching would demonstrate the presence of numerous number of certain connective tissue cell]. Answer the following:

The stain characteristic for this cell is:
questions.explanation: Toluidine blue shows mast-cell granule metachromasia; trypan blue is macrophage vital stain, Sudan lipid, silver reticular/Golgi and orcein elastic.

questions.text: Elastic fibers are formed by the following cells:
questions.explanation: Fibroblasts synthesize elastic fibers. Distinguishing alternatives: Macrophage defense; Fat storage; Mast mediators; Plasma antibodies.

questions.text: Histiocytes are the most common type of cells in the connective tissue.
questions.explanation: Fibroblasts are the most common CT proper cells.

questions.text: Fibrocytes have deeply basophilic cytoplasm and euchromatic nucleus.
questions.explanation: Inactive fibrocytes have pale scant cytoplasm and dark condensed nuclei.

questions.text: Fat droplets in fat cells can be demonstrated by Sudan III stain.
questions.explanation: Sudan III demonstrates lipid preserved in frozen sections.

questions.text: Multilocular fat cells are brown in color due to presence of melanin pigments in their cytoplasm.
questions.explanation: Brown fat color reflects mitochondrial cytochromes and vascularity, not melanin.

questions.text: Many lysosomes of different types (primary and secondary) are present in the cytoplasm of macrophages.
questions.explanation: Macrophages have abundant lysosomal compartments involved in uptake/digestion.

questions.text: Reticular cells are rounded in shape.
questions.explanation: Reticular cells are branched cells with processes.

questions.text: Accumulation of excess tissue fluid in the extracellular space is called Scurvy.
questions.explanation: Excess extracellular fluid is edema; scurvy is vitamin C deficiency affecting collagen.

questions.text: Plasma cells originate from differentiation of B-lymphocytes.
questions.explanation: Activated B lymphocytes differentiate into plasma cells.

questions.text: The cytoplasm of mast cells is filled with coarse granules.
questions.explanation: Mast cytoplasm contains abundant coarse basophilic granules.

questions.text: Collagen fibers are basophilic.
questions.explanation: Collagen is acidophilic with eosin staining.

questions.text: Reticular fibers are arranged into wavy branching bundles formed of non- branching fibers.
questions.explanation: That description is type I collagen bundles; reticular fibers themselves branch into networks.

questions.text: Collagen type II is present in the skin, tendons, ligaments and bones.
questions.explanation: Those listed sites are predominantly type I collagen; type II is cartilage.

questions.text: Collagen type IV is present in the basal lamina.
questions.explanation: Basal lamina contains type IV collagen.

questions.text: Loose areolar connective tissue is present everywhere in the body except the lungs.
questions.explanation: Loose CT occurs around vessels/nerves and in lung supporting interstitium; lungs are not an excluded organ.

questions.text: Loose areolar connective tissue allows exchange of nutrients to and from blood vessels.
questions.explanation: Hydrated loose CT and interstitial fluid allow nutrient/metabolite exchange around vessels.

questions.text: Adipose connective tissue contains fat cells only.
questions.explanation: Adipose contains CT septa, reticular fibers, vessels, nerves and stromal cells in addition to adipocytes.

questions.text: Brown adipose connective tissue is rich in blood supply.
questions.explanation: Rich capillary supply contributes to brown fat color and heat transfer.

questions.text: Mucoid connective tissue contains elastic fibers.
questions.explanation: Designated book lists few collagen, elastic and reticular fibers in mucous CT.

questions.text: Match Column (A) with Column (B).
questions.explanation: Use characteristic fibroblast basophilia, macrophage lysosomes, reticular branching, mast metachromasia and plasma clock-face nucleus.

pairs.target: Darkly basophilic cytoplasm and pale nucleus
Rich in different types of lysosomes
Stellate shaped with many long processes

questions.text: Match Column (A) with Column (B).
questions.explanation: Type I collagen is prominent in the dermis, type II in cartilage, and type IV in basal lamina networks. Orcein demonstrates elastic fibers; silver impregnation demonstrates the delicate type III reticular network.

questions.text: The cell derived from B lymphocytes is:
questions.explanation: B lymphocytes differentiate into plasma cells.

questions.text: The connective tissue is characterized by:
questions.explanation: Connective tissue contains relatively dispersed cells within abundant extracellular matrix.

questions.text: Collagen fibers are mainly synthesized by :
questions.explanation: Fibroblasts synthesize the collagen-rich extracellular matrix of connective tissue proper.

questions.text: which one of the following can be stained metachromatically by toludine blue :
questions.explanation: Sulfated components of mast-cell granules produce metachromasia with toluidine blue.

questions.text: This cell can be vitally stained :
questions.explanation: Macrophages phagocytose vital dyes such as trypan blue administered to living tissue.

questions.text: plasma cells secrete:
questions.explanation: Plasma cells contain extensive rough endoplasmic reticulum for immunoglobulin synthesis and secretion.

questions.text: Mast cells secrete:
questions.explanation: Mast-cell granules contain both histamine and heparin, making the combined option the best answer.

questions.text: Which one of the following C.T cells is typically an antigen presenting cell:
questions.explanation: Macrophages are professional phagocytic antigen-presenting cells among these options.

questions.text: Which one of the following C.T cells, its nucleus has a clock face appearance:
questions.explanation: Clock-face heterochromatin identifies plasma cells.

questions.text: Which one of the following C.T cells has receptors for immunoglobulin E (IgE):
questions.explanation: Mast cells bear the characteristic high-affinity IgE receptors.

questions.text: Pericytes of the connective tissue arises from:
questions.explanation: The course describes pericytes as descendants of undifferentiated mesenchymal cells surrounding small vessels.

questions.text: Under certain conditions, Pericytes of the connective tissue can differentiate into:
questions.explanation: The designated course book describes injury-associated pericyte differentiation into fibroblasts, smooth muscle cells, and endothelial cells.

questions.text: The ground substance of connective tissue is synthesized mainly by:
questions.explanation: Active fibroblasts synthesize ground-substance components as well as connective-tissue fibers.

questions.text: Yellow elastic fibers are stained:
questions.explanation: Orcein stains elastic fibers reddish brown and highlights their branching elastic network.

questions.text: The stroma of the organs is formed by:
questions.explanation: Fine type III reticular networks support organ parenchymal cells.

questions.text: which type of CT fibers is stained by silver:
questions.explanation: Reticular fibers are argyrophilic and become visible with silver impregnation.

questions.text: which cell is present around blood capillaries:
questions.explanation: Pericytes partly surround capillary and small-venule endothelium and share its basement-membrane region.

questions.text: Which types of adipose cells is a characteristic for newborns:
questions.explanation: Brown adipose tissue is prominent in newborns and helps protect them against cold through heat production.

questions.text: Unilocular fat cells :
questions.explanation: A single large lipid droplet pushes the unilocular adipocyte nucleus to the edge and leaves a thin rim of cytoplasm.

questions.text: Irregular white fibrous connective tissue is seen in:
questions.explanation: Organ capsules contain dense irregular collagen bundles that resist stresses in multiple directions.

questions.text: Brown adipose connective tissue is:
questions.explanation: Brown adipose tissue consists of multilocular adipocytes specialized for producing heat.

questions.text: Tendon is formed of :
questions.explanation: Parallel type I collagen bundles in tendons withstand repeated tensile force along one principal direction.

questions.text: yellow elastic connective tissue is present in:
questions.explanation: Ligamentum nuchae is rich in elastic fibers, supporting stretch followed by recoil.

questions.text: Reticular connective tissue is present in:
questions.explanation: Reticular connective tissue provides a supporting framework in organs such as lymph nodes, spleen, liver, and bone marrow.

questions.text: which of the following connective tissues, its ground substance is jelly like and formed mainly of hyaluronic acids:
questions.explanation: Wharton's jelly is a mucous connective tissue with abundant hydrated ground substance rich in hyaluronic acid.

questions.text: Type I collagen is present mainly in :
questions.explanation: Dense connective tissue contains abundant type I collagen arranged in thick bundles.

questions.text: Which one of the connective tissue cell can differentiate into endothelial cell?
questions.explanation: The designated notes identify pericytes as multipotential perivascular cells able to form endothelial cells.

questions.text: The following cells are types of macrophages EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Fibrocytes are quiescent matrix-producing cells, not monocyte/macrophage-derived phagocytes.

questions.text: One site for corresponding type of macrophages is NOT correct:
questions.explanation: Microglia reside in the central nervous system rather than bone marrow.

questions.text: The followings are members of mononuclear phagocytic system EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: White connective tissue is a tissue type, not a member of the phagocyte cell system.

questions.text: Russell bodies are spherical inclusion present in:
questions.explanation: Russell bodies are immunoglobulin accumulations in plasma cells.

questions.text: After staining the C.T with toludin blue the cells which have magenta granules are:
questions.explanation: Mast-cell sulfated granules stain metachromatically with toluidine blue.

questions.text: After staining of collagen fibers:
questions.explanation: H&E stains collagen pink; Van Gieson collagen is red rather than green.

questions.text: What are stretchable/flexible CT fibers?
questions.explanation: Elastic fibers stretch and recoil.

questions.text: C.T is classified into C.T proper and specific C.T according to:
questions.explanation: Classification reflects cells and the composition and organization of extracellular matrix, including fibers.

questions.text: The most widespread C.T is:
questions.explanation: Loose areolar connective tissue is the widely distributed packing and supporting tissue.

questions.text: Loose areolar C.T is abundant in:
questions.explanation: Papillary superficial dermis contains loose areolar connective tissue.

questions.text: Dense C.T:
questions.explanation: Dense connective tissue contains abundant fibers with relatively fewer cells.
options: Has more cells and few fibers.
Has more fibers and few cells.
Has few cells and huge amount of matrix.
Has few fibers and huge amount of matrix.

questions.text: Macrophages originate from..?
questions.explanation: The designated monocyte-derived tissue macrophages arise from blood monocytes.

questions.text: Collagen is secreted by all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Fibroblasts, osteoblasts and chondroblasts produce collagen matrix; mast cells release inflammatory mediators.

questions.text: All of the following are true about yellow elastic fibers EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Elastic fibers are branching stretchable fibers, stained with orcein and only weakly eosinophilic in routine H&E.

questions.text: Which of the following cells is the precursor of histamine & heparin.?
questions.explanation: Mast cells store and release histamine and heparin.

questions.text: All of the following is branched Connective tissue cells EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Plasma cells are rounded or oval rather than the branching stromal cells.

questions.text: Plasma cells:
questions.explanation: Plasma cells arise from activated B cells, possess clock-face nuclei and occur in connective and lymphoid tissues.
options: Formed by B lymphocytes activated by antigen.

questions.text: The connective tissue is characterized by:
questions.explanation: The general connective-tissue description includes vascularity, separated cells and abundant extracellular matrix; specialized cartilage is an avascular exception.

questions.text: Yellow elastic fibers are stained:
questions.explanation: Orcein stains elastic fibers brown and the designated Van Gieson description gives them yellow.

questions.text: Reticular fibers can be stained by the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Reticular fibers are demonstrated by silver and PAS, rather than distinctly with routine H&E.

questions.text: Concerning collagen fibers:
questions.explanation: Individual collagen fibers are unbranched and form wavy branching bundles; they are stainable with Van Gieson.
options: they are wavy branching bundles formed of non branching fibers.
they stain with van Gieson stain.

questions.text: Dermis of skin is formed of:
questions.explanation: Papillary dermis is loose connective tissue and reticular dermis is dense irregular collagenous tissue.

questions.text: ALL those connective tissue cells are branched Except:
questions.explanation: Adipocytes are rounded rather than branching cells.

questions.text: Staining of the macrophage with trypan blue is an example of:
questions.explanation: Trypan blue administration to living animals demonstrates macrophage uptake as vital staining.

questions.text: Collagen type III forms:
questions.explanation: Type III collagen forms reticular parenchymal stromal networks.

questions.text: The following are found in basal lamina EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Basal lamina contains laminin and type IV collagen, while type II chiefly occurs in cartilage.

questions.text: The following are types of macrophages EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Merkel cells are sensory epithelial cells, not macrophages.

questions.text: About macrophages all are true EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Macrophages do not derive from B lymphocytes; the latter differentiate into plasma cells.
options: Stained with vital staining using trypan blue.
Stained histochemically using acid phosphatase technique.

questions.text: Reticular fibers all are true except:
questions.explanation: Type III reticular fibers form fine parenchymal stromal networks; organ capsules mainly contain dense type I collagen.
options: Form the capsule of cellular organs (parenchymatous organs)

questions.text: One of the following cells is derived from monocyte:
questions.explanation: Monocytes can become tissue macrophages; plasma cells instead derive from B lymphocytes.

questions.text: Collagen fibers of CT are:
questions.explanation: Fibroblasts are major collagen-producing cells and collagen is protein, not Sudan-stained lipid.
options: Present as one type of fibers

questions.text: Dense regular CT is present in:
questions.explanation: Parallel collagen bundles resist tension along the tendon axis.

questions.text: Cells responsible for producing the components of the CT intercellular substance:
questions.explanation: Fibroblasts synthesize connective-tissue fibers and ground-substance components.

questions.text: Elastic fibers can be demonstrated by using:
questions.explanation: Orcein binds elastic tissue, whereas Sudan III demonstrates fat.

questions.text: White collagenous fibers are characterized by:
questions.explanation: Unbranched collagen fibers aggregate into wavy bundles that resist tension.

questions.text: Immunoglobulin E is attached to receptors on the surface of:
questions.explanation: IgE binds the characteristic high-affinity mast-cell receptors involved in immediate hypersensitivity.

questions.text: this type of CT support parenchyma cells in the organs:
questions.explanation: Fine reticular networks support parenchymal cells while permitting close vascular and cellular interactions.

questions.text: Origin of smooth muscle cells:
questions.explanation: Smooth muscle generally develops prenatally from undifferentiated mesenchymal cells. Distinguishing alternatives: Fibroblasts are matrix cells; Ectoderm is not the general smooth-muscle origin; Endoderm is not the general origin.

questions.text: Intermediate fibers forming cytoskeleton of smooth muscles:
questions.explanation: Desmin is present in smooth muscle and vimentin in vascular smooth muscle; the combined option covers both.

questions.text: Smooth muscle cells are connected by:
questions.explanation: Gap junctions transmit signals between smooth muscle cells. Distinguishing alternatives: Tight junction seals; Adherens junction anchors; Junctional complex is the epithelial apical complex.

questions.text: Which of the following structures are responsible for calcium regulation in the smooth muscle cells?
questions.explanation: Caveolae help regulate calcium flux at the smooth-muscle surface. Distinguishing alternatives: Actomyosin contracts; Dense bodies anchor filaments; Gap junctions communicate; Intermediate filaments support.

questions.text: An old age heavy smoker man presented to the clinic with atherosclerotic plaques in his aorta and coronary arteries. What is the source of collagen fibres present in these plaques?
questions.explanation: The designated course describes vascular smooth-muscle proliferation and collagen production contributing to atherosclerotic plaques.

questions.text: Neutrophiles characterized by the following except:
questions.explanation: Neutrophils have segmented multilobed nuclei; a bilobed nucleus is characteristic of eosinophils. Distinguishing alternatives: 3-5 nuclear lobes is supported; Neutrophilic granules are supported; Acute bacterial inflammation involves neutrophils.

questions.text: Fixed cells of bone marrow include the following except:
questions.explanation: Megakaryocytes are developing hematopoietic cells producing platelets, rather than fixed stromal cells.

questions.text: In adults, Red ( active ) bone marrow is present in the following except:
questions.explanation: Adult long-bone shafts predominantly contain yellow marrow; active red marrow remains in axial bones and proximal long-bone ends.
options: Shaft = diaphysis of the long bones

questions.text: Origin of blood platelets:
questions.explanation: Platelets are cytoplasmic fragments derived from marrow megakaryocytes. Distinguishing alternatives: Mesenchymal cells are not the immediate source; Pericytes are mural cells; Monocytes produce macrophages.

questions.text: Responsible for blood Grouping:
questions.explanation: ABO antigenic determinants are carbohydrates exposed on the red-cell surface glycocalyx. Distinguishing alternatives: Cytoskeleton supports shape; Cholesterol modulates membrane properties; Phospholipids alone are not ABO determinants.
options: Cell coat on outer surface of RBCs
Cytoskeleton on the inner surface of RBCs plasma membrane

questions.text: Responsible for RBCs Elasticity:
questions.explanation: The submembranous cytoskeletal network gives RBCs mechanical support and deformability. Distinguishing alternatives: Cell coat carries surface antigens; Cholesterol affects membrane fluidity but is not the principal elastic scaffold; Phospholipids form bilayer rather than scaffold.
options: Cell coat on outer surface of RBCs
Cytoskeleton on the inner surface of RBCs plasma membrane

questions.text: Which of the following leucocytes migrate to the connective tissue and differentiate into a cell that is positively stained for acid phosphatase enzyme?
questions.explanation: Monocytes become lysosome-rich macrophages demonstrable by acid-phosphatase histochemistry. Distinguishing alternatives: Neutrophils do not differentiate into macrophages; Basophils do not become macrophages; Lymphocytes are a different lineage; Platelets are fragments.

questions.text: The thickest layer in medium sized arteries:
questions.explanation: Muscular arteries have a thick tunica media with smooth muscle and elastic elements. Distinguishing alternatives: Intima is inner layer; Adventitia is relatively thinner; Submucosa is not a vascular wall layer.

questions.text: The thickest layer in medium sized veins:
questions.explanation: Medium veins have relatively thin media and thick adventitia. Distinguishing alternatives: Intima is thin; Media is relatively thin; Submucosa is not a vascular coat.

questions.text: Internal elastic lamina is present in:
questions.explanation: A well-developed internal elastic lamina marks muscular arteries. Distinguishing alternatives: Veins lack the developed lamina; Capillaries lack three wall coats; Sinusoids lack muscular-artery coats.

questions.text: Fenestrated blood capillaries are present in:
questions.explanation: Fenestrated capillaries occur where rapid exchange/filtration occurs, including kidney, intestine and endocrine organs.

questions.text: Blood sinusoids are present in the following except:
questions.explanation: Marrow, spleen and liver have sinusoids; intestinal mucosa has fenestrated capillaries. Distinguishing alternatives: Marrow is a sinusoid site; Spleen is a sinusoid site; Liver is a sinusoid site.

questions.text: Blood sinusoids of bone marrow are characterized by which of the following:
questions.explanation: Marrow sinusoids are wide irregular channels with discontinuous endothelial/basal-lamina barriers. Distinguishing alternatives: Channels are irregular; Channels are wide; Endothelium is discontinuous; Continuous basal lamina is false.
options: Have no or discontinuous basement membrane,

questions.text: The outer layer of the intrapulmonary bronchus contains...
questions.explanation: Bronchial adventitia contains hyaline cartilage plates, muco-serous glands and lymphoid tissue. Distinguishing alternatives: Pure serous misstates mixed glands; Pure mucous misstates mixed glands; Omits lymphoid tissue and misstates gland type; Omits mixed gland and lymphoid description.
options: Hyaline cartilage, serous glands & lymphoid follicles.
Hyaline cartilage, mucous glands & lymphoid follicles.
Hyaline cartilage, muco-serous glands & lymphoid follicles.
Hyaline cartilage, serous glands & plexus of nerves.
Hyaline Cartilage, mucous glands & plexus of nerves

questions.text: Which of the following structures is NOT a part of the blood-air barrier
questions.explanation: The thin blood-air barrier includes type-I epithelium, fused basal lamina and capillary endothelium; type-II cells secrete surfactant instead.

questions.text: Surfactant is formed by:
questions.explanation: Type-II pneumocytes synthesize and secrete pulmonary surfactant. Distinguishing alternatives: Macrophages remove debris; Type-I cells exchange gases; Cartilage supports airways; Endothelium lines vessels.

questions.text: Terminal part of the conductive portion of respiratory tract:
questions.explanation: Terminal bronchioles end the conducting zone before alveolated respiratory bronchioles. Distinguishing alternatives: Respiratory bronchioles start exchange zone; Alveolar ducts belong to exchange zone; Alveoli belong to exchange zone.

questions.text: Respiratory portion of respiratory tract include the following except:
questions.explanation: Terminal bronchioles are conducting passages without the respiratory-zone alveoli. Distinguishing alternatives: Respiratory bronchioles are exchange zone; Alveolar ducts are exchange zone; Alveoli/sacs are exchange zone.

questions.text: Bronchi are lined by:
questions.explanation: Bronchial respiratory lining is pseudostratified ciliated columnar with goblet cells. Distinguishing alternatives: Simple columnar does not describe larger bronchial respiratory lining; Stratified columnar is not normal bronchial lining; Squamous forms alveolar surface; Clara/club cells characterize bronchioles.
options: Pseudostratified columnar ciliated epithelium with goblet cells

questions.text: Clara cells are present in the lining of:
questions.explanation: Club cells, historically Clara cells, occur in bronchiolar epithelium. Distinguishing alternatives: Alveoli have pneumocytes; Trachea has respiratory lining with goblet cells; Bronchi have respiratory lining.

questions.text: Glomerular capillaries are:
questions.explanation: Glomerular endothelial fenestrations lack diaphragms, unlike the podocyte filtration slits which have slit diaphragms.

questions.text: Cells forming the visceral layer of Bowman’s capsule are:
questions.explanation: Podocytes form the visceral epithelial layer around glomerular capillaries. Distinguishing alternatives: Endothelium lines inside capillaries; Cuboidal cells line tubular segments; Pericytes are mural cells.

questions.text: Podocytes are attached to glomerular capillaries by:
questions.explanation: Podocyte secondary foot processes rest on the glomerular basal lamina. Distinguishing alternatives: Body is displaced from filtration surface; Primary processes give rise to foot processes; Nucleus does not attach to capillary wall.

questions.text: 2ry processes of podocytes are separated by:
questions.explanation: Secondary podocyte pedicles interdigitate, leaving filtration slits spanned by thin slit diaphragms.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT true about podocytes?
questions.explanation: Filtration slits lie between secondary pedicles, not primary podocyte processes. Distinguishing alternatives: Modified squamous description is supported; Primary and secondary processes are supported; Slits between pedicles are supported; Thin slit diaphragms are confirmed by the opened glomerular TEM atlas.
options: Filtration slits are present between their pedicles.
Filtration slits are covered by diaphragm.
Filtration slits are present between their 1ry processes

questions.text: Portal tract area contains branches of……..
questions.explanation: Portal tracts contain portal-vein, hepatic-artery and bile-duct branches plus lymphatics. Distinguishing alternatives: Central vein is in lobule center; Central vein is not portal tract; Hepatic vein is not the portal-triad vessel; Portal artery is not the named vessel.
options: Hepatic artery, central vein & bile duct.
Central vein, portal vein & bile duct.
Hepatic vein, portal vein & bile duct.
Hepatic artery, portal vein, bile duct.
Hepatic vein, portal artery & bile duct.

questions.text: Mass of liver tissue from 2 classic hepatic lobules , the cells of which surround the same vascular core:
questions.explanation: A liver acinus spans adjoining classic lobules around a shared terminal vascular supply. Distinguishing alternatives: Portal lobule is organized around bile drainage; Bile lobule is not the named vascular unit; Functional lobule is not the specific course term.

questions.text: Triangular part of liver tissue draining bile into the same bile duct:
questions.explanation: Portal lobules combine portions of three classic lobules draining to one portal bile duct. Distinguishing alternatives: Acinus is perfusion-oriented; Bile lobule is not the listed course term; Classic lobule centers on a central vein.

questions.text: Zone of liver acinus most affected in case of hypoxia:
questions.explanation: Zone 3 lies furthest from the incoming arterial blood and is most vulnerable to hypoxia. Distinguishing alternatives: Zone 1 receives oxygen-rich blood first; Zone 2 is intermediate; Zones are not equally vulnerable.

questions.text: All about liver sinusoids is true except:
questions.explanation: Sinusoids receive portal-vein and hepatic-artery blood and drain toward central veins. Distinguishing alternatives: Fenestrated endothelium/Kupffer lining is supported; Space of Disse separates lining and hepatocytes; Basal barrier is discontinuous.
options: Lined by fenestrated endothelium & Kupffer cells
Endothelial cells are separated from hepatocytes by (space of Disse)= (perisinusoidal space)
Contain blood from central vein only

questions.text: Types of borders of hepatocytes:
questions.explanation: Hepatocytes have sinusoidal, bile-canalicular and intercellular surface domains. Distinguishing alternatives: Generic epithelial labels omit sinusoidal/canalicular organization; Luminal is nonspecific; Peripheral/central do not name the functional liver domains.

questions.text: thyroid gland stores its secretion in form of:
questions.explanation: Thyroid hormone precursors are stored extracellularly in follicular colloid as thyroglobulin. Distinguishing alternatives: Intracytoplasmic granules are not main thyroid storage; Extracellular colloid is not discrete secretory granules; Neither granule option is the accurate storage form.

questions.text: cells responsible for decreasing serum Ca level
questions.explanation: Parafollicular C cells secrete calcitonin, which lowers blood calcium. Distinguishing alternatives: Follicular cells secrete T3/T4; Parathyroid chief cells increase calcium through PTH; Basophil cells are not the thyroid calcium-lowering population.

questions.text: Basophils:
questions.explanation: Basophils release histamine and heparin in allergic responses.

questions.text: Mature Erythrocytes:
questions.explanation: Mature mammalian erythrocytes lack nuclei and organelles.

questions.text: Eosinophils have the following characters EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Eosinophils have a bilobed nucleus and large acidophilic granules, and participate in antiparasitic responses.
options: their number increases in parasitic infection.

questions.text: B-lymphocytes have the following characters EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: B cells have rounded nuclei rather than the kidney-shaped nucleus of monocytes.

questions.text: In connective tissue mature monocytes differentiate to:
questions.explanation: Blood monocytes migrate into tissues and can differentiate into macrophages.

questions.text: Basophils:
questions.explanation: Basophils have irregular S-shaped nuclei, large basophilic granules and release histamine/heparin.

questions.text: The followings cells are involved in the allergic reaction:
questions.explanation: Basophils release allergic mediators and eosinophils modulate allergic responses.

questions.text: The following statements concerning B-lymphocyte are true EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: B cells develop in bone marrow; thymus is the maturation site for T cells.
options: The main responsible for humoral immunity.

questions.text: Red bone marrow:
questions.explanation: Red marrow is active hematopoietic tissue found widely in newborn bones.
options: active found in cavities of bones of newborns.
Inactive found in shaft of long bones in adults.
has a high content of fat cells.

questions.text: In the smooth muscle cells, caveolae means:
questions.explanation: Caveolae are small plasma-membrane invaginations involved in calcium handling.
options: Vesicular invaginations of the cell membrane.

questions.text: The following filaments present in the smooth muscle cells EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Smooth muscle contains actin, myosin and intermediate filaments; collagen fibrils are extracellular matrix.

questions.text: Following statements concerning smooth muscle are true EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Smooth muscle cells are fusiform acidophilic cells with one central nucleus.
options: The cells are fusiform in shape.
The length of cells varies from 30 μm to 500 μm.

questions.text: The tunica intima is formed of the followings EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Intima consists of endothelium, basement membrane and subendothelial connective tissue; skeletal muscle is absent.

questions.text: Internal elastic lamina can be detected in:
questions.explanation: Internal elastic lamina lies at the outer boundary of intima adjacent to media.

questions.text: Smooth muscle fibers abundant in:
questions.explanation: Tunica media is the main smooth-muscle layer of blood vessels.

questions.text: Section in the aorta shows the following histological features EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Aortic media has numerous elastic lamellae, not only a few.
options: Little number of elastic laminae in the tunica media.
Smooth muscle fibers in the tunica media.

questions.text: Veins have:
questions.explanation: Veins have relatively poorly developed elastic laminae and a relatively thick adventitia compared with their media.

questions.text: Blood sinusoids:
questions.explanation: Sinusoids occur in liver, spleen and marrow and have a discontinuous wall and basement membrane.
options: They are present in the liver, bone marrow and spleen.
Pericytes are present along its wall.

questions.text: which cell is normally found only in bronchioles:
questions.explanation: Clara or club cells are characteristic bronchiolar secretory cells.

questions.text: The alveoli are present in all of the following parts of respiratory tract EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Terminal bronchioles are conducting passages without alveoli in their wall.

questions.text: Concerning Type II pneumocytes, all are true EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Type II cells chiefly secrete surfactant and regenerate alveolar epithelium; type I forms the thin diffusion barrier.

questions.text: Bronchi:
questions.explanation: Intrapulmonary bronchi have supporting hyaline-cartilage plates, smooth muscle and respiratory epithelium with cilia and goblet cells.
options: have plates of hyaline cartilage in their wall.

questions.text: The follicular cells of thyroid gland are normally characterized by all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Follicular cells secrete thyroid hormones and usually are cuboidal with basophilic synthetic cytoplasm; apical cilia are absent.

questions.text: The thyroid gland is characterized by all the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Thyroid is endocrine; its colloid is an intrafollicular hormone precursor store rather than exocrine secretion.

questions.text: The follicular cells of thyroid gland all the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Follicular cells have developed protein-synthetic and endocytic organelles rather than abundant lipid storage.

questions.text: All the following are true about the parafollicular cells of thyroid gland EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: C cells contain hormone-secretory granules.
options: They are larger than follicular cells.
They are rounded with central spherical nuclei.
They cannot reach the lumen of the follicle.

questions.text: Thyroid parafollicular cells secrete:
questions.explanation: Thyroid C cells synthesize calcitonin.

questions.text: The cells of the visceral layer of renal corpuscles are called:
questions.explanation: Podocytes form the visceral layer covering glomerular capillaries.

questions.text: The glomeular capillaries:
questions.explanation: Glomerular endothelium is fenestrated without diaphragms and rests on continuous thick basement membrane.
options: are lined by simple cuboidal epithelium.
are surrounded by continuous basement membrane.

questions.text: Renal corpuscle is formed of:
questions.explanation: Renal corpuscle includes Bowman capsule, glomerular capillary tuft and supporting mesangial cells.

questions.text: Meissner’s plexus is present in:
questions.explanation: Meissner plexus lies in submucosa.

questions.text: The liver acinus:
questions.explanation: The acinus is modeled as a diamond-shaped territory around terminal vascular branches.
options: is a diamond shaped mass of liver tissue.

questions.text: The hepatocytes:
questions.explanation: Hepatocytes are polygonal cells with developed smooth ER and acidophilic cytoplasm.

questions.text: The liver acinus is characterized by:
questions.explanation: A diamond-shaped acinus spans parts of two adjacent classic lobules around terminal vascular branches.
options: A diamond shaped mass of liver tissue.
A portal tract is located in its center.
Parts of three adjacent classic hepatic lobules.

questions.text: “Concretions” are found in which of the following glands?
questions.explanation: Corpora amylacea are characteristic prostatic luminal concretions.

questions.text: The epithelial lining of the endcervix of the uterus:
questions.explanation: Endocervical canal is lined by mucus-secreting simple columnar epithelium.

questions.text: The basal layer of uterine endometrium:
questions.explanation: The basal layer is supplied by straight arteries and persists during menstruation.

questions.text: Yellow bone marrow:
questions.explanation: Yellow marrow is relatively inactive, fat-rich tissue in adult long-bone shafts.
options: active found in cavities of bones of newborns.
Inactive found in shaft of long bones in adults.
has a high content of fat cells.

questions.text: Fenestrated basement membrane are present in:
questions.explanation: Discontinuous basement membrane characterizes sinusoids; fenestrated capillaries have endothelial pores with continuous basal lamina.

questions.text: Skeletal muscle has:
questions.explanation: Skeletal muscle contains continuous capillaries.

questions.text: The brain has:
questions.explanation: Cerebral capillaries have continuous endothelium contributing to the blood-brain barrier.

questions.text: Glomerular capillaries are:
questions.explanation: Glomerular endothelium is fenestrated.

questions.text: Endocrine glands have:
questions.explanation: Endocrine glands generally have fenestrated capillaries for hormone exchange.

questions.text: The liver has:
questions.explanation: Liver parenchyma is perfused by sinusoids.

questions.text: Preterminal bronchioles are lined by:
questions.explanation: The designated description gives ciliated simple columnar epithelium in preterminal bronchioles.

questions.text: Adventitia of bronchioles contains:
questions.explanation: Bronchioles lack cartilage plates, submucosal glands and the bronchial lymphoid-follicle layer.

questions.text: Alveolar sac is lined by:
questions.explanation: Alveolar sacs comprise groups of thin-walled alveoli and are conventionally classified as simple squamous lining.

questions.text: Concerning Type I pneumocytes, all are true EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Type I cells are thin squamous gas-exchange cells; type II cells secrete surfactant.

questions.text: The lateral borders of follicular cells have:
questions.explanation: Lateral borders have junctional complexes.

questions.text: The apical surface of follicular cells have:
questions.explanation: Follicular cells have apical microvilli and apically situated secretory vesicles.

questions.text: Auerbach’s plexus is present in:
questions.explanation: Auerbach myenteric plexus lies within muscularis externa between its layers.

questions.text: Muscularis muosa is present in:
questions.explanation: Muscularis mucosae is the smooth-muscle component of mucosa.

questions.text: The portal lobule:
questions.explanation: The portal lobule is a triangular territory centered on a portal bile duct.
options: is a diamond shaped mass of liver tissue.
is hexagonal mass of liver tissue.

questions.text: The classic hepatic lobule:
questions.explanation: Classic hepatic lobule is roughly hexagonal, centered on a central vein with portal tracts peripherally.
options: has a portal tract in the periphery.
has a central vein in the center.

questions.text: The portal tract contains branches from all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Portal tracts contain portal-vein branches, hepatic-artery branches and bile ducts, not hepatic-vein branches.

questions.text: The space of Disse is:
questions.explanation: Space of Disse lies between hepatocytes and sinusoidal endothelium.
options: Located between blood sinusoids & portal tract.

questions.text: The bile canaliculi is:
questions.explanation: Canaliculi are channels formed between adjacent hepatocytes.
options: Located between blood sinusoids & portal tract.
located between adjacent hepatocytes within the liver plate.

questions.text: The blood sinusoid is:
questions.explanation: Sinusoids lie between hepatocyte plates and associate with fenestrated/discontinuous endothelial cells and Kupffer cells.
options: Located between blood sinusoids & portal tract.
located between adjacent plates of hepatocytes.
lined with fenestrated endothelial cells & kupffer cells.

questions.text: Concerning the hepatocytes, all of the following is true EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Hepatocytes have three functional surface domains, not four, in the designated description.

questions.text: which of the following organelles is abundant in hepatocytes:
questions.explanation: Hepatocytes have abundant rough ER, smooth ER and peroxisomes for their diverse metabolic functions.

questions.text: The exocrine function of liver is:
questions.explanation: Bile secretion is the exocrine liver function.

questions.text: The renal corpuscle has:
questions.explanation: Renal corpuscle has vascular and urinary poles.

questions.text: The Bowman’s capsule has:
questions.explanation: Bowman capsule has parietal and visceral layers.

questions.text: All of the following is a part of the nephron EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The nephron includes renal corpuscle, proximal/distal tubules and loop; collecting ducts belong to the collecting system.

questions.text: The cells of the parietal layer of renal corpuscle are:
questions.explanation: Parietal Bowman capsule is simple squamous epithelium.

questions.text: concerning podocytes, all of the following are true EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Podocyte pedicels form filtration slits bridged by slit diaphragms.
options: Its filtration slits are covered by diaphragm.
Its filtration slits are not covered by diaphragm.

questions.text: The glomerular basement membrane is formed of:
questions.explanation: The filtration basement membrane is shared between glomerular endothelium and podocytes.

questions.text: The glomerular basement membrane is:
questions.explanation: Glomerular basement membrane is continuous and unusually thick despite endothelial fenestrations.

questions.text: Cell coat is:
questions.explanation: The glycocalyx is an extracellular carbohydrate coat, so it is PAS positive. It contains glycoproteins and glycolipids; cholesterol is the main membrane-stability factor.
options: Present on the inner surface of plasma membrane
important factor for stability of plasma membrane

questions.text: …………… is the main factor for stability of cell membrane
questions.explanation: Cholesterol stabilizes the phospholipid bilayer and moderates its fluidity.

questions.text: Peripheral membrane proteins
questions.explanation: Peripheral proteins associate loosely with the membrane surface and help support the cytoskeleton.
options: more on the outer surface of plasma membrane
its function is support for cytoskeleton

questions.text: Plasma membrane in E.M. appear as:
questions.explanation: At electron-microscope resolution a unit membrane has two dense lines separated by a lighter zone.

questions.text: Thickness of the cell membrane:
questions.explanation: The plasma membrane is approximately 7-10 nanometres thick, well below ordinary light-microscope resolution.

questions.text: Functions of cell coat include the following Except:
questions.explanation: The cell coat participates in recognition, adhesion, and receptor functions; peripheral membrane proteins support the cytoskeleton.

questions.text: Inner mitochondrial membrane
questions.explanation: Oxidative-phosphorylation enzymes occupy the inner mitochondrial membrane and its cristae.
options: has cristae which carry respiratory enzymes

questions.text: Mitochondria
questions.explanation: Mitochondria accumulate near sites of high ATP consumption, including the apical region of ciliated cells.
options: present in apical cytoplasm in ciliated cells.

questions.text: About Mitochondrial matrix, all the following is true Except
questions.explanation: Respiratory-chain enzymes are associated with the inner mitochondrial membrane rather than the matrix.

questions.text: Mitochondria with tubular cristae characterizes which of the following cells?
questions.explanation: Tubular cristae characterize steroid-secreting cells.

questions.text: Cholesterol in cell membrane:
questions.explanation: Cholesterol molecules are interspersed among phospholipids in both leaflets of the plasma membrane.
options: present in the outer phospholipid layer only
present in the inner phospholipid layer only
projects on the outer cell surface

questions.text: ………………………….Is an example of active transport
questions.explanation: Ion pumps couple solute movement to an energy source and can transport against a concentration gradient.

questions.text: Cells rich in sER include:
questions.explanation: Muscle cells have specialized smooth endoplasmic reticulum that stores and releases calcium for contraction.

questions.text: sER by light microscope
questions.explanation: Smooth ER lacks attached ribosomes and does not form the conspicuous basophilic regions seen with rough ER.

questions.text: rER:
questions.explanation: Ribosomes on rough ER produce localized basophilia in cells engaged in protein secretion.
options: appear as localised basophilia by light microscope
appear as diffuse basophilia by light microscope
form cytoplasmic proteins for cell use

questions.text: negative Golgi appearance with H&E can be seen in:
questions.explanation: Plasma cells have an unstained perinuclear negative Golgi region in routine H&E.

questions.text: Cis face of Golgi apparatus is related to:
questions.explanation: The cis, or immature, Golgi face receives transfer vesicles budding from rough ER.

questions.text: Functions of rER include:
questions.explanation: Rough-ER-bound ribosomes synthesize secreted proteins and deliver them into ER cisternae.

questions.text: Modification of secretory proteins occurs in:
questions.explanation: Golgi cisternae modify, sort, and package proteins arriving from rough ER.

questions.text: One of the following vesicles has its membrane from Golgi apparatus:
questions.explanation: Secretory vesicles bud from the trans face of the Golgi apparatus and carry concentrated products for release.

questions.text: digestion of old organelle occurs through:
questions.explanation: Autophagy delivers worn-out intracellular organelles to lysosomes for digestion in autophagolysosomes.

questions.text: Lysosomes can be demonstrated by:
questions.explanation: Histochemical localization of acid phosphatase demonstrates lysosomes because they contain acid hydrolases.

questions.text: Organelle which can multiply by fission:
questions.explanation: Mitochondria renew themselves by growth and fission, using their own genetic machinery.

questions.text: microtubules are forms of:
questions.explanation: Microtubules are assembled from tubulin subunits into thirteen protofilaments around a hollow core.

questions.text: free ribosomes forms:
questions.explanation: Free ribosomes principally synthesize cytosolic proteins and proteins imported into selected organelles.

questions.text: …………….Appear as diffuse basophilia:
questions.explanation: Abundant free ribosomes or polysomes can produce diffuse cytoplasmic basophilia.

questions.text: glycogen stored in cytoplasm can be stained with:
questions.explanation: PAS histochemistry demonstrates glycogen as purple or magenta-positive cytoplasmic material.

questions.text: Heterochromatin:
questions.explanation: Heterochromatin is compact chromatin composed of DNA associated with histone and other proteins.

questions.text: Inner & outer nuclear membranes are continuous at:
questions.explanation: The inner and outer nuclear membranes join at the margins of nuclear pores.

questions.text: ………………is an example of histochemical staining:
questions.explanation: Acid-phosphatase histochemistry localizes lysosomal enzyme activity through a specific reaction.

questions.text: Basal body of cilia is formed of:
questions.explanation: A ciliary basal body contains nine peripheral triplets of microtubules. The shaft instead has nine doublets and two central singlets in the usual motile axoneme.

questions.text: Core of microvilli is formed of:
questions.explanation: The structural core of a microvillus consists of bundled actin microfilaments, also called thin filaments.

questions.text: in paraffin technique , fixation is performed by :
questions.explanation: Formaldehyde fixation preserves tissue architecture before dehydration and embedding.

questions.text: aim of fixation include the following except:
questions.explanation: Removal of tissue water is the purpose of dehydration, rather than fixation.
options: increase the affinity of tissue to stain

questions.text: example of histochemical stain:
questions.explanation: PAS is a chemical reaction used to demonstrate glycogen within tissue sections.
options: staining of macrophage with trypan blue
staining of mast cell with toluidine blue
staining of Golgi with silver stain

questions.text: clearing done by:
questions.explanation: Xylol clears the specimen by replacing alcohol with an agent miscible with paraffin.

questions.text: sectioning of slides from paraffin section:
questions.explanation: Routine paraffin sections are cut with a microtome at approximately 5-8 micrometres for light microscopy.
options: occurs with microtome , slide thickness 5-8 um
occurs with microtome , slide thickness 50-80 um
occurs with ultra microtome , slide thickness 50-80 um
occurs with ultra microtome , slide thickness 5-8 um

questions.text: Which of the following structures can deliver proteins synthesized by ribosomes of rER to the Golgi apparatus?
questions.explanation: Transfer vesicles carry rER proteins to the cis Golgi. Distinguishing alternatives: Coated vesicles is less specific than the named transfer pathway; Pinocytotic vesicles internalize fluid; Phagosomes contain particles; Secretory vesicles exit trans Golgi.

questions.text: Lysosomal enzymes are active at which of the following pH?
questions.explanation: The designated book specifies an acidic lysosomal lumen near pH 5 maintained by proton pumps. Distinguishing alternatives: 4 is more acidic than the stated course lumen; 6 resembles early endosomes; 7 is near-neutral; 8 is alkaline.

sourceOccurrences.sourceFile: McQs/formative Exam 2 for intro to hist.pdf
sourceAliases: McQs/formative Exam 2 for intro to hist.pdf

questions.text: Lysosomes are specifically stained using which of the following techniques?
questions.explanation: Acid-phosphatase histochemistry demonstrates lysosomal enzyme activity. Distinguishing alternatives: Immunostaining can target proteins but is not the stated activity demonstration; Culture is growth technique; Vital staining demonstrates living-cell uptake; Supravital refers to living cells outside the body.

sourceAliases: McQs/formative Exam 2 for intro to hist.pdf

questions.text: Which of the following organelles are concerned with oxidation of toxic metabolites within the cell?
questions.explanation: Peroxisomes contain oxidative enzymes that metabolize potentially toxic substances. Distinguishing alternatives: Lysosomes hydrolyze material; Proteasomes degrade proteins; Endosomes sort cargo; Phagosomes contain engulfed particles.

sourceOccurrences.sourceFile: McQs/formative Exam 2 for intro to hist.pdf
sourceAliases: McQs/formative Exam 2 for intro to hist.pdf

questions.text: Mitotic cyclins are rapidly inactivated and degraded by which of the following organelles
questions.explanation: Proteasomes degrade short-lived regulatory proteins including mitotic cyclins. Distinguishing alternatives: Endosomes sort cargo; Lysosomes degrade endocytic/autophagic cargo; Phagosomes contain particles; sER regulates lipids/calcium.

sourceOccurrences.sourceFile: McQs/formative Exam 2 for intro to hist.pdf
sourceAliases: McQs/formative Exam 2 for intro to hist.pdf

questions.text: Outer aspect cell membrane differs from inner aspect in the presence of….
questions.explanation: The glycocalyx is exposed only on the extracellular membrane surface. Distinguishing alternatives: Peripheral proteins occur on both surfaces; Cholesterol occurs in both leaflets; Integral proteins occupy membrane regions; Both leaflets contain phospholipids.

questions.text: Which of the following is considered an aim of fixation?
questions.explanation: Fixation preserves structure and increases stain affinity; gradual dehydration prevents shrinkage. Distinguishing alternatives: Gradual dehydration prevents shrinkage; Clearing produces transparency; Fixation hardens tissue; Sectioning allows transmission.
options: Increase affinity of tissue to stain

questions.text: Which of the following parts of the light microscope is responsible for collection and focusing of light?
questions.explanation: The condenser collects and focuses light on the specimen. Distinguishing alternatives: Objective forms/enlarges image; Ocular enlarges image for viewer; Electron beam is an EM source; Diaphragm controls aperture rather than collects light.

questions.text: Which of the following structures can identify a TEM of adrenal cortex?
questions.explanation: Steroid-secreting adrenal cortical cells characteristically contain mitochondria with tubular cristae.

questions.text: Compare between vital and supravital stains and give example for each?
questions.explanation: Vital staining colors living cells in vivo: injected trypan blue is engulfed by macrophages. Supravital staining colors living cells removed from the body in vitro: Janus green B stains mitochondria in fresh cells.
questions.modelAnswer: Vital staining colors living cells in vivo: injected trypan blue is engulfed by macrophages. Supravital staining colors living cells removed from the body in vitro: Janus green B stains mitochondria in fresh cells.

questions.text: Describe the pathways of digestive materials into lysosomes?
questions.explanation: Extracellular material enters by phagocytosis or pinocytosis and its vesicle/endosomal compartment joins lysosomes for digestion (heterophagy). Intracellular worn organelles are enclosed in autophagosomes which fuse with lysosomes (autophagy). Digested products enter cytosol; indigestible remnants persist as residual bodies or undergo exocytosis.
